papers.title: The MHC requirement for αβ T-cell specification is heterochronically gated
papers.authors: Sun, X.; Ma, F.; Zak, A. J.; Bogle, R. B.; Correa-Medero, L. O.; Fallouh, H. G.; Rudak, P. T.; Rizvi, S. M.; Vanderzee, I. O.; Schmerk, C.; Chen, L.; Haeryfar, S. M. M.; Eaton, K. A.; Carty, S. A.; Wen, F.; Billi, A. C.; Tsoi, L. C.; Gudjonsson, J. E.; Laouar, A.; Laouar, Y.
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-dependent thymic selection is a defining principle of {beta} T-cell development, yet mice lacking {beta}2m-dependent MHC class I and MHC class II retain rare {beta} T cells whose developmental significance has remained unresolved. Here we show that this residual compartment is not simply the product of failed selection. Single-cell and clonotypic profiling resolves distinct outcomes, including clonally restricted CD4-associated states and a diversified CD8 {beta} T-cell population that converges on physiological wild-type virtual memory. These CD8 cells lack conventional self-MHC calibration, retain broad T-cell receptor (TCR) diversity, respond rapidly to T-cell receptor and cytokine stimulation, and confer protection during bacterial infection. Their preservation is developmentally restricted: the MHC-independent state carries a neonatal transcriptional and phenotypic imprint, is favored by fetal but not adult progenitors, and is reduced by neonatal Lin28 inhibition. While these data do not displace the central requirement for MHC in generating the conventional naive {beta} T-cell repertoire, they establish that {beta} T-cell specification can proceed during early life in its absence, yielding a physiological and functionally competent CD8 {beta} T-cell fate. Thus, the MHC requirement for {beta} T-cell specification is heterochronically gated.

papers.title: One-carbon metabolism-derived prognostic signature orchestrates reactive oxygen species redox homeostasis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic profiling.
papers.authors: Li C, Chen Y, Xu L, Gong Z, Ni Y.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated onecarbon metabolism drives tumor progression and redox homeostasis by modulating reactive oxygen species balance, yet robust onecarbon metabolismderived prognostic biomarkers for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to identify prognostic one-carbon metabolism-related genes in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, dissect their multi-layer molecular regulatory networks, including reactive oxygen species redox homeostasis, and elaborate novel reactive oxygen species-centered mechanistic insights into head and neck squamous cell carcinoma pathogenesis prognostic biomarkers. The Cancer Genome Atlas-head and neck squamous cell carcinoma dataset was processed via DESeq2 to screen differentially expressed genes between head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and matched normal tissues. Candidate one-carbon metabolism-associated genes were obtained by intersecting differentially expressed genes with canonical one-carbon metabolism gene sets. The predictive performance of the model was validated in the Cancer Genome Atlas internal validation cohort, the full aggregated the Cancer Genome Atlas head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cohort, and the external Gene Expression Omnibus dataset GSE65858. In total, 8261 differentially expressed genes and 132 one-carbon metabolism-related candidate genes were filtered out. Eight hub prognostic genes (HPRT1, SFXN3, SMS, ADA, NT5E, TXNRD1, GATM, and SCLY) were screened to construct a one-carbon metabolism-derived risk signature. The model exhibited favorable predictive efficacy with all area under the curve values ≥ 0.6 across all independent validation cohorts. Patients assigned to the high-risk group presented markedly inferior overall survival, particularly those with Stage IV advanced disease and N1+2 lymph node metastasis. The high-risk subgroup showed enhanced tumor immune escape, remodeled immune cell infiltration profiles, extensive chemotherapeutic resistance, and disrupted intracellular reactive oxygen species homeostasis dominated by upregulated TXNRD1-mediated antioxidant signaling that eliminates cytotoxic reactive oxygen species and supports tumor survival under oxidative stress. Single-cell RNA sequencing further confirmed epithelial cells as the primary cell subpopulation expressing all eight signature genes, which exerted stage-specific dynamic transcriptional patterns along epithelial pseudotime trajectories to coordinate one-carbon metabolism flux, reactive oxygen species clearance, immune suppression, and malignant progression. The eight-gene one-carbon metabolism prognostic signature possesses robust and stable capacity for predicting the overall survival of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and are closely correlated with tumor therapeutic responsiveness.

papers.title: OSM‑mediated STAT3/PDL1 promotes tumor progression and immune escape in colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Shi Y, Duan J, Wang Z, Lin H, Zhen H, Tang B, Cao B.
papers.abstract: Despite considerable progress in the clinical management of colorectal cancer (CRC), immune evasion remains a persistent challenge. Oncostatin M (OSM) expression and immune cell infiltration in CRC was first characterized using publicly available databases and clinical specimens. CRC cell lines with OSM overexpression were then established and their tumor‑promoting functions were assessed via in vitro proliferation, migration and wound healing assays. Subsequently, bulk RNA sequencing coupled with bioinformatic analysis was performed on human CRC cell lines, complemented by single cell RNA sequencing in a C57BL/6 mouse model. Subsequently, expression‑based ligand‑receptor analysis was used to investigate bidirectional communication between tumor and myeloid cells. Finally, flow cytometry and western blotting were subsequently used to evaluate programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD‑L1) expression, T‑cell‑associated exhaustion markers, STAT3 phosphorylation, and the effects of pharmacological STAT3 inhibition. It was demonstrated that OSM expression was elevated in CRC tissues, and public‑dataset analysis associated higher OSM expression with poorer overall survival. OSM overexpression enhanced proliferative and migratory phenotypes in HCT116 and RKO cells. Single‑cell analysis revealed changes in the relative abundance of tumor, stromal and immune‑cell populations following OSM overexpression. Ligand‑receptor analysis further identified selective remodeling of bidirectional tumor‑myeloid communication, including increased predicted SPP1‑, MIF‑, CCL‑, TWEAK‑ and OSM‑associated signaling. OSM‑OSMR/IL6ST communication was detected in both tumor‑to‑myeloid and myeloid‑to‑tumor directions in the OSM‑overexpressing (OE) group. OSM overexpression was also associated with increased PD‑L1 expression, enhanced STAT3 phosphorylation, reduced CD8 + T‑cell representation, and increased PD‑1 and TIM‑3 expression in the analyzed tumor sample. In separate short‑term Stattic‑treated experiments, STAT3 inhibition remained lower STAT3 phosphorylation in OSM‑OE CRC cells. In conclusion, OSM overexpression is associated with enhanced malignant phenotypes, selective remodeling of tumor‑myeloid communication, and activation of STAT3/PD‑L1‑related signaling in CRC. These findings support an OSM‑associated model of tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune regulation, while further functional and molecular studies are required to establish the causal contribution of individual myeloid subsets and the direct dependence of PD‑L1 induction on STAT3.

papers.title: Resident liver macrophages buffer dietary and circulating cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis
papers.authors: Hamilton, M.; Morshed, S. M.; Chlebowski, M.; Shiau, C. E.
papers.abstract: Cholesterol metabolism is viewed largely through the lens of hepatocytes, leaving the roles of other liver cells unclear. Using high-resolution live imaging and cholesterol tracing in intact zebrafish, complemented by genetic and clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion and single-cell analysis, we identify liver-resident macrophages (LMs) as cellular buffers of circulating and dietary cholesterol. LMs directly take up cholesterol, and their depletion redirects cholesterol to hepatocytes, which suppress cholesterol synthesis, increase bile-acid synthesis and efflux, and activate metabolic-stress and immune programs, including hepatokine lect2 induction. These responses are heightened by elevated dietary cholesterol and occur without overt inflammation or altered liver architecture. LMs partition cholesterol through abca1b-dependent export and cetp-mediated lipoprotein remodeling. Loss of abca1b causes cholesterol sequestration in LMs and reduced cholesterol-processing demand on hepatocytes, while LM depletion eliminates macrophage-derived cetp and reduces hepatocyte cetp. Together, these findings reveal the innate immune system as integral to normal metabolic physiology, with LMs buffering cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis.

papers.title: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats
papers.authors: Ni, M.; He, Z.; Han, X.; Zhu, Y.; Gong, X.; Wang, W.; Wang, P.; Luo, J.; Wang, W.; Yi, G.; Li, C.
papers.abstract: Milk production requires coordinated remodeling of mammary epithelial lineages and their stromal and immune niches, but this process is incompletely resolved in dairy goats. We aim to define period specific cell states and epithelial niche interactions across the dry to lactation transition. We profile mammary tissue from three peak-lactation and three dry-period Saanen goats using 10x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing and map one peak-lactation goat with Stereo-seq. Among 44,120 cells, we identify15 populations. Peak lactation is characterized by expansion of luminal alveolar cells and increased {beta}-casein and -lactalbumin expression, whereas luminal progenitors, hormone-sensing cells, fibroblasts, and B cells are enriched in the dry period. Trajectory inference place luminal progenitors near branches toward alveolar and hormone-sensing states, with sustained ELF5-associated activity along the alveolar branch. Myoepithelial, macrophage, natural killer T, and T cell states are also remodeled. SPP1 and MIF signaling networks become more connected and change their cellular targets. These data establish a period resolved atlas of dairy goat mammary remodeling and identify coordinated epithelial, stromal, immune, and communication programs associated with active lactation.

papers.title: A Beta-to-Alpha seasonal coronavirus antibody signature identifies high and low responders to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination
papers.authors: Longet, S.; Brady, C.; Tomic, I.; Tipton, T.; Bessalah, S.; Barnes, E.; Dunachie, S.; Duncan, C. J.; Klenerman, P.; Richter, A.; Thaventhiran, J. E.; Turtle, L.; de Silva, T. I.; Tomic, A.; Carroll, M. W.
papers.abstract: Pre-existing immunity to endemic seasonal human coronaviruses may shape subsequent responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We longitudinally profiled 775 healthcare workers using a systems immunology machine learning framework and found that a recursive feature elimination cross-validation model classified individuals in the top and bottom quartiles of SARS-CoV-2 Spike IgG responses (AUC=0.72, empirical P<0.001). This predictive signature was prominently driven by a baseline bias toward Beta-coronavirus relative to Alpha-coronavirus Spike reactivity.

papers.title: Kidney fibrosis mechanisms in the single‑cell era: From cellular heterogeneity to therapeutic opportunities (Review).
papers.authors: Wang Y, Yang D, Liu N, Zeng H.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease affects >13% of adults worldwide, yet no approved antifibrotic therapy is available. Recent advances in single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the understanding of renal fibrosis. These technologies have unmasked unexpected heterogeneity among myofibroblasts and macrophages, identified scar‑associated macrophage subsets and resolved the long‑standing debate over myofibroblast origins by confirming resident fibroblasts as the principal source. Spatial transcriptomics has further defined functional communities and pathologically distinct niches, including maladaptive repair niches centred on SOX9+ epithelial cells, profibrotic microenvironments enriched in tenascin‑C and immune‑activation niches where macrophages and fibroblasts co‑localize. Intercellular crosstalk networks involving TGF‑β, NOTCH and paracrine signals from injured tubules have been systematically mapped. These insights are now being translated into targeted strategies, such as surface marker‑directed agents against CD248 and fibroblast activation protein, epigenetic modulators including HDAC6 inhibitors and advanced 3D bioprinted human models. The present review synthesized these single‑cell and spatial discoveries to provide a conceptual framework for developing precision antifibrotic therapies for progressive kidney disease.

papers.title: Associating p-phenylenediamine and p-toluenediamine with AML using a network toxicology-based approach.
papers.authors: Yang X, Li J, Yang G, Tian X, Zhang X, Liu J.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a prevalent acute hematological malignancy among adults, notable for its unfavorable prognosis and relatively low survival rates. Evidence suggests prolonged exposure to substandard permanent hair dyes containing hazardous chemical agents may elevate cancer risk, including AML. However, the precise mechanisms underlying this carcinogenic association remain elusive. This research identified p-phenylenediamine (PPD) and p-toluenediamine (PTD), primary constituents of hair dyes, as highly carcinogenic substances potentially implicated as key drivers of AML linked to hair dye usage. Targets relevant to PPD and PTD were predicted using databases such as ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, STITCH, and PharmMapper. Additionally, AML-related targets were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and GeneCards databases. Core genes were isolated using weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis confirmed the predictive accuracy of these critical targets. Immune cell infiltration analysis further elucidated potential associations between these targets and the AML immune microenvironment. To verify compound-target interactions and stability, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted. Our computational predictions suggest that PPD/PTD may directly target PTPRC, suggesting a potential mechanism by which these compounds disrupt immune microenvironment homeostasis and could promote AML progression. These findings suggest that PPD/PTD exposure could promote AML progression, which warrants experimental validation.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling identifies a CXCL9-PD-1 + CD8 + T cell axis for prediction of checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis.
papers.authors: Bi N, Jiang Z, Yang Y, Xie J, Liu Z, Jiang Y, Sun S, Zhang Q, Liu S, Zhong D, Wu L, Wang M, Zhang C, Zhang T, Wang J, Yu H, Cheng G, Xi G, Zhou X, Gao Y.
papers.abstract: Background Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a life-threatening complication of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). We aimed to identify predictive biomarkers associated with symptomatic CIP (sCIP) and unravel the underlying pathogenesis. Methods We integrated CyTOF, proteomics, single-cell RNA and V(D)J sequencing, single-cell secretomics, and spatial transcriptomics. These techniques were used to profile peripheral blood, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and lung tissue samples from two prospective multi-center cohorts of NSCLC patients receiving ICI combination treatments. Results Elevated serum CXCL9 levels combined with high frequencies of peripheral PD-1 + CD8 + T cells after induction ICI were associated with subsequent sCIP (AUC=0.954) and inferior overall survival (HR=7.19, p=0.004). Mechanistically, PD-1 + CD8 + T cells displayed a type 1 effector profile characterized by IFN-γ and MIP-1β secretion. CXCL9/CXCR3 signaling was associated with recruitment of these cells to inflamed lung tissue. Conclusions The CXCL9-PD-1 + CD8 + T cell axis is associated with CIP pathogenesis. This mechanism supports a potential blood-based biomarker model for CIP risk stratification and identifies a promising preventive therapeutic target to optimize clinical management.

papers.title: Checkpoint Inhibition during primary hepatitis E virus infection alters memory development of virus-specific T-cells in humans.
papers.authors: Kelsch L, Arnold J, Maas M, Borkmann M, Rafei D, Rusignuolo G, Llewellyn-Lacey S, Price DA, Bengsch B, Hofmann M, Thimme R, Neumann-Haefelin C, Sagar, Boettler T.
papers.abstract: Background & aims HEV infection is an underappreciated differential diagnosis in patients presenting with acute hepatitis during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. As T-cells are the key targets of ICIs, particularly through blockade of inhibitory immune checkpoints such as PD-1, this intervention is likely to influence the dynamics and differentiation fate of de novo primed virus-specific T-cells during primary HEV infection. We therefore aimed to examine how PD-1 blockade during primary HEV-infection influences expansion, contraction, and memory formation of virus-specific CD8+ T-cells. Methods HEV-specific CD8 and CD4+ T-cells were analyzed by applying a reverse phenotyping approach combined with single-cell transcriptomics and TCR sequencing, as well as multiparameter flow cytometry with MHC class I tetramers. We characterized HEV-specific T-cell responses in patients receiving ICI and in untreated patients during acute-viremic infection and after viral clearance. Results Under ICI, de novo primed HEV-specific CD8+ T-cells showed enhanced clonal expansion, cytotoxicity, and terminal differentiation. Rather than transitioning into classical memory subsets, these cells retained a cytotoxic transcriptional program and acquired features of long-lived effector-like T-cells (LLEC). While HEV-specific T-cells remained detectable over > 2 years, their functional recall responsiveness declined in ICI-treated patients. Conclusions Collectively, our findings demonstrate that PD-1 blockade during the formation of a primary immune response reshapes the fate of the antiviral CD8+ T-cell pool, favoring terminally differentiated effector states over conventional memory formation, with potential implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies. Lay summary Our study represents the first demonstration in a human model that PD-1 blockade during primary antigen exposure reshapes antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector formation and memory differentiation. By identifying PD-1 signaling during a primary immune response as a regulator of antiviral CD8+ T-cell fate, our findings establish a conceptual framework for understanding how immune checkpoint blockade influences the development of primary antiviral T-cell responses, with implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Citrus-derived hesperidin ameliorates immune-metabolic and immuno-fibrotic dysfunction in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: multi-omics and single-cell insights.
papers.authors: Wu X, Zhang Y, Zhou L, Tao L, Tan X, Zhao L, Liu M, Tang T.
papers.abstract: Hesperidin (HES), a citrus flavanone, was tested in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) using multi-omics and single-cell frameworks. Five-week-old mdx mice received HES (10/20 mg kg-1) orally for 4 weeks. HES improved grip strength, reduced immobility, and alleviated muscle fragility. Histopathology showed better myofiber organization and less inflammation and collagen levels. Network pharmacology identified 56 overlapping targets with enhanced inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis. Bulk RNA-seq revealed transcriptional reprogramming, restoration of mitochondrial respiratory chain components (NDUFA/B/C and COX6A1) and suppression of chemokines (CCL2 and CCL7) and fibrotic markers (COL1A1 and POSTN). GSEA confirmed oxidative phosphorylation reactivation (mdx vs. WT, NES = -3.41; H10 vs. mdx, NES = 2.91) and reversal of glycolysis-inflammation signatures. Untargeted metabolomics showed remodeling in creatine, arginine, glutathione, and acyl-carnitine pathways, with key metabolites (creatine, guanidinoacetic acid, succinate, and fumarate) shifted toward WT. Integrated analysis converged on oxidative phosphorylation, arginine and proline metabolism, and immune signaling. Single-cell RNA-seq showed HES reduced inflammatory macrophages, attenuated fibrotic differentiation, rebalanced B/T cells, and suppressed pathogenic signaling (TGF-β, THBS, and periostin). Western blot analysis confirmed inhibition of TGF-β/Smad2/3 and NF-κB axes (reducing collagen, TGF-β, p-Smad2/3, α-SMA, and p-p65 levels) and restored GPX4/SLC7A11; immunofluorescence showed reduced M1 (iNOS) infiltration. Deep single-cell analyses showed HES shifted macrophages from pro- to anti-inflammatory branches, switching regulons from Spi1/Irf8/Stat1/Rel to Nfkb1/Stat6/Maf/Atf4; virtual Tgfb1-knockout confirmed partial involvement of the TGF-β1 pathway. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, HES suppressed iNOS/CD86 as effectively as dexamethasone. Collectively, HES confers multi-layered protection across function, tissue, metabolism, immune-fibrotic networks, and intercellular signaling, supporting its potential as a food-derived adjunct targeting the secondary consequences of dystrophin deficiency.

papers.title: HPV-associated macrophage states and expression-based scores in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Li Y, Huang Z, Wang A.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) status defines contrasting immune ecosystems in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We investigated how tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) states and their regulatory programs contribute to this diversity and whether these features can be captured in patient-level expression signatures. We integrated 229,196 single cells from 59 patients with HNSCC (26 HPV-positive and 33 HPV-negative), defined eight TAM states, and combined functional and trajectory analyses with regulon inference, virtual perturbation, and CellChat. A 12-gene Weighted Inflammatory Score (WIS) and a TAM-related score (TRS) were evaluated in independent transcriptomic cohorts. Multiplex immunofluorescence provided representative tissue-level observations. HPV-positive tumors showed a lymphoid-enriched landscape, whereas HPV-negative tumors had greater TAM and fibroblast representation. Patient-level comparisons identified lower Inflammatory TAM and Pro-tumor/Secretory TAM fractions in HPV-positive patients (Benjamini-Hochberg [BH]-adjusted p = 0.0172 and 0.0486, respectively). Regulon analysis and virtual SNAI1 perturbation converged on inflammatory, leukocyte migration, and chemotaxis programs. Targeted CellChat analysis identified a candidate epithelial-source HLA-DRA-CD4 interaction involving seven TAM recipient states in HPV-positive tumors compared with two in HPV-negative tumors. Fixed-coefficient WIS achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.938 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.863-1.000) across 36 independent patients. TRS provided complementary HPV-status discrimination, with a cross-validated AUC of 0.783 in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and an external AUC of 0.649 in GSE40774. HPV-associated immune differences in HNSCC involve distinct macrophage states, candidate SNAI1-linked inflammatory and migratory regulatory programs, and inferred epithelial-TAM communication patterns. WIS and TRS connect selected single-cell observations with patient-level transcriptomic features and may guide future mechanistic and validation studies.

papers.title: Human CD47 Expression on Porcine Endothelial Cells Regulates Natural Killer Cell Function via SIRPα.
papers.authors: Tran T, Kemter E, Galdina V, Kartmann H, Mahesh A, Zhang X, Urquidi O, Galvão DR, Pereira SF, Gigli M, Grimus S, Kurome M, Zakhartchenko V, Kessler B, Yang K, Lickert H, Wolf E, Reichart D, Puga Yung GL, Seebach JD.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are pivotal in xenograft rejection, targeting porcine endothelial cells. CD47 acts as a "don't eat me" signal by binding to signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPα),suppressing immune activation. While this axis has been well characterized in macrophages, its influence on NK cell-mediated xenograft rejection remains unclear. We investigated whether expression of human CD47 (hCD47) on porcine aortic endothelial cells (PAECs) from transgenic pigs inhibits human NK activity. Under static conditions, hCD47 expression on PAECs significantly reduced direct NK cytotoxicity. In microfluidic systems simulating physiological conditions, GGTA1-KO/hCD47-TG PAECs were associated with reduced NK cell-mediated lysis and motility compared with WT PAECs. However, with heat-inactivated human plasma containing anti-pig non-αGal antibodies, hCD47 expression did not protect αGal-knockout PAECs from NK cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed overall homogeneous NK subtype distribution between WT and hCD47-expressing PAEC conditions. However, a small set of differentially expressed genes showed increased inhibitory receptor expression and reduced effector, activation, and proliferation signatures in NK cells exposed to hCD47. These findings identify hCD47 as an effective checkpoint against direct NK cytotoxicity, but insufficient to prevent ADCC, underscoring the need for combinatorial strategies to achieve durable protection from NK-driven xenograft rejection.

papers.title: CENPT Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Progression by Activating the RAF/MEK/ERK Signaling Pathway and Triggering MIF-Mediated Immunosuppression.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Yin X, Yin C, Hu C, Li J, Wang C, Xu Q, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies, with its incidence and mortality rates remaining particularly discouraging. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving PDAC progression and identifying potential therapeutic targets are critical to improve the clinical prognosis of PDAC patients. Accumulating evidence has highlighted the pivotal functions of centromere proteins (CENPs) in tumor progression. Accordingly, this study aimed to screen and identify key CENP family members implicated in PDAC pathogenesis. Through systematic analysis of CENP family proteins in PDAC, we identified CENPT as a critical regulator involved in disease progression. We further validated that CENPT promoted the proliferation and metastasis of PDAC cells via activating the RAF/MEK/ERK signaling pathway through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments. In addition, CENPT was also found to be implicated in tumor microenvironment remodeling. Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses demonstrated that CENPT expression was positively correlated with Treg cell abundance and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Further experiments suggested that CENPT upregulated the synthesis and secretion of MIF in PDAC cells, which acted on naive CD4 + T cells to promote the differentiation into Treg cells. This process ultimately induced the formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and facilitated PDAC progression, whereas blockade of MIF enhanced the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade for PDAC. In conclusion, this study revealed the crucial role of CENPT in PDAC progression, and targeting CENPT may serve as one of the potential therapeutic strategies for PDAC.

papers.title: Advances in data-driven taxonomy of innate immune cells.
papers.authors: Bonavita E, Mantovani A, Garlanda C.
papers.abstract: Single-cell technologies, coupled with powerful machine learning, have multiplied the number of named innate immune cell states faster than their biological features have been established. Innate cell identity is generated by at least four partially independent axes (ontogeny, maturation, response to microbial or damage signals, and tissue adaptation) that project onto a shared transcriptional space. Consequently, snapshot expression data alone cannot uniquely attribute an observed partition to any one of these processes. Data-driven taxonomy has been particularly effective where one axis provides a stable interpretative anchor, as in ontogeny-defined conventional dendritic cells, and faces greater challenges where several axes interact, as in granulocytes, tissue-adapted macrophages, and ILCs. Here, we assess what recent atlas and foundation model studies have resolved, identify independent biological validation rather than computational resolution as the current bottleneck, and propose an explicit evidence hierarchy for deciding when computational clusters should be considered bona fide biological entities.

papers.title: Integrating multi-omics data and experimental validation to elucidate the therapeutic mechanism of the Ephedra-Cinnamomi Ramulus pair in psoriasis.
papers.authors: Wang SS, Zhang Q, Zhang RH, Chen F, Liu Q, Liu YJ, Liu J, Liu C, Guo S.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease driven by complex immune microenvironments, and the Ephedra-Cinnamomi Ramulus pair (EHCR) has shown therapeutic potential but its mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, by integrating network pharmacology, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and experimental validation, we show that, in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced mouse model, EHCR alleviates psoriasiform dermatitis during a seven-day IMQ/gavage regimen, with inflammatory fibroblasts nominated as a candidate cell population by target-score analysis. Mechanistically, EHCR suppresses the nuclear factor kappa B subunit 1 (NFKB1)/RELB, NF-κB subunit (RELB)/DExD-box helicase 21 (DDX21) signaling axis, wherein the canonical p50/p65 complex and RelB-containing non-canonical NF-κB complex may regulate DDX21 transcription, and this axis is hyperactivated in psoriatic fibroblasts. Two candidate bioactive constituents of EHCR, quercitrin and 3,3',4',5,7-pentahydroxyflavanone, showed measurable binding to p50 and RelB proteins in SPR assays and were associated with reduced NFKB1/RELB/DDX21 signaling in fibroblasts. Furthermore, EHCR attenuates GJA1-dependent, contact-dependent communication between fibroblasts and dendritic cells, with reduced gap junction protein alpha 1 (GJA1) expression and the abundance of dendritic cells adjacent to fibroblasts. Collectively, these findings suggest that EHCR attenuates IMQ-induced psoriasiform dermatitis during the seven-day IMQ/gavage regimen, in association with reduced NFKB1/RELB/DDX21 signaling in fibroblasts and attenuated GJA1-dependent, contact-dependent fibroblast-DC communication. The mechanism underlying these associations and their translational relevance remain to be established.

papers.title: CD47-dependent myeloid reprogramming drives IL-10-mediated T-cell suppression in heatstroke.
papers.authors: Feng Z, Gong Z, Wang S, Xiang X, Wang L, Wang L, Gao C, Xiao F, Liao X, Ma C, Yang J, Shi L, Zhang X, Wu Q, Wang B, Kang Y, He M, Zhang Z, Zhang W.
papers.abstract: Heatstroke can trigger immune dysregulation, yet the mechanisms driving progression to critical illness remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing with functional studies to characterize heatstroke-associated immunosuppression. Transcriptomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from heatstroke patients revealed a transition from enhanced innate immune responses in mild heatstroke to marked adaptive immune suppression in critical disease. Disease progression was associated with increased S100A8/A12 and IL-10 expression and reduced T-cell- and HLA-associated gene expression. Myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) signatures correlated inversely with CD8⁺ T-cell abundance and cytotoxicity and positively with IL-10 levels and disease severity. Single-cell analyses revealed depletion of T and NK cells, myeloid expansion, MDSC accumulation, and reduced T-cell clonality. Pseudotime and RNA velocity analyses further indicated that heatstroke redirects myeloid differentiation towards an immunosuppressive MDSC state. In mice, CD47 blockade restrained MDSC expansion and IL-10 production, restored T-cell function, reduced organ injury, and improved survival. These findings identify myeloid reprogramming and MDSC-mediated T-cell suppression as mechanisms of heatstroke-associated immune dysfunction and support CD47 blockade as a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: SHMT2 K280 Succinylation Drives Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma Progression via S100A8 + Neutrophil-Mediated Immunosuppression.
papers.authors: Zha Q, Cheng C, Liang S, Zhang Y, Zhang W, Tao S, Han S, Sun L, Wei W, Liu Y, Ma K, Chu J, Zhang N, Deng S, Liu Y, Wang J, Liu L.
papers.abstract: Background: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) remains therapeutically challenging due to its aggressive biology and highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). While the contribution of protein succinylation to immune evasion is increasingly recognized, the specific succinylation events governing immunosuppression in ICC are poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate how succinylation drives TME remodeling to promote ICC progression and to identify potential therapeutic targets for improving patient outcomes. Methods: Succinyl-proteomic analysis of 10 pairs of ICC tumor tissues and adjacent normal tissues revealed that succinylation of serine hydroxymethyltransferase 2 (SHMT2) at lysine 280 (K280) was increased in ICC tumor tissues compared with paired adjacent normal tissues. Immunoprecipitation combined with mass spectrometry was used to identify lysine acetyltransferase 2A (KAT2A) as the enzyme mediating SHMT2 K280 succinylation. Subcutaneously implanted tumor models and hydrodynamic transfection-induced ICC models were used to investigate the in vivo role of SHMT2 K280 hyper-succinylation. Single-cell RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and in vitro functional assays were conducted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms through which SHMT2 K280 succinylation remodels the TME. Results: We observed a significant elevation of SHMT2 K280 succinylation in clinical ICC specimens and identified this modification as a critical posttranslational modification that drove immunosuppression through a nonenzymatic signaling axis. Mechanistically, KAT2A-mediated SHMT2 K280 hyper-succinylation inhibited the proteolysis of FOS (Fos proto-oncogene, AP-1 transcription factor subunit), thereby enhancing FOS-mediated regulation of lipocalin-2 (LCN2) expression. Secreted LCN2 subsequently recruited and activated neutrophils expressing S100 calcium-binding protein A8 (S100A8) by binding to its receptor, solute carrier family 22 member 17 (SLC22A17). Neutrophil infiltration established an immunosuppressive microenvironment niche that potently impaired CD8 + T cell function and promoted tumor progression. Disruption of the SHMT2-LCN2 axis abrogated neutrophil-mediated immunosuppression and enhanced the efficacy of chemotherapy and immunotherapy in preclinical ICC models. Conclusions: We propose that combining LCN2 blockade with either gemcitabine/cisplatin or immune checkpoint inhibitors represents a precision strategy for ICC patients harboring SHMT2 K280 hyper-succinylation. Our work reveals a noncanonical, succinylation-driven mechanism by which SHMT2 modulates the immune landscape, and identifies LCN2 blockade as a therapeutically actionable target to increase the efficacy of both chemotherapy and immunotherapy in ICC.

papers.title: Long-read nanopore sequencing: A rapid and highly accurate approach for IGHV gene analysis in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia.
papers.authors: Del Peso Santos T, Rabbani L, Ioannou A, Österholm C, Hägerstrand D, Mansouri L, Rosenquist R.
papers.abstract: The somatic hypermutation (SHM) status of the immunoglobulin heavy variable (IGHV) gene is a key prognostic and predictive biomarker in chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL). Current methods, including Sanger sequencing and short-read next-generation sequencing, are accurate but have limitations in scalability and turnaround time. Here, we present an integrated workflow for multiplexed long-read nanopore sequencing of full-length IGHV-IGHD-IGHJ rearrangements, leveraging recent advances in sequencing chemistry and base calling. Peripheral blood samples from 60 patients with CLL, representing diverse IGHV subgroups and SHM levels, were analysed. Single-step polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification with EuroClonality-based primers and simultaneous barcoding enabled multiplexing of 12 samples per run. Sequencing on the MinION platform generated over 200 000 high-quality (≥Q30) reads per sample after quality filtering. A dominant productive clonotype was identified in all cases (mean abundance 75%). Comparative analysis demonstrated high concordance with Illumina-based results for IGHV-IGHD-IGHJ gene usage and SHM status. Secondary rearrangements with a frequency of >5% were consistently detected across platforms. The workflow enabled a turnaround time below 24 h at an estimated cost of approximately €70 per sample. In summary, these findings establish long-read sequencing as a rapid, accurate and cost-effective method for full-length IGHV gene SHM assessment, supporting its implementation in routine clinical diagnostics.

papers.title: Discovery, design, and applications of environment-responsive antibodies.
papers.authors: Jansen T, Jacobsen CP, Gosvig T, Tulika T, Sørensen CV, Jensen MB, Jenkins TP, Ljungars A, Laustsen AH.
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies typically bind their targets independently of the local biological environment. Depending on the target and therapeutic application, this can lead to on-target, off-tumor toxicity, target-mediated clearance, and suboptimal intracellular trafficking. Environment-responsive antibodies address these limitations by modulating antigen binding in response to pH, metal-ion concentrations, or metabolite gradients. This can enable preferential target engagement in acidic tumors, promote antigen release in acidic endosomes to enable FcRn-mediated recycling of the unbound antibody, or increase transit across the blood-brain barrier through pH-responsive binding to the transferrin receptor. This review covers display-based selection technologies, rational structure-guided design, and computational approaches for discovering environment-responsive antibodies. We highlight the therapeutic applications of environment-responsive antibodies and discuss their emerging role in improving context-dependent target engagement and pharmacokinetics.

papers.title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer: a multicentre development, validation, and testing study.
papers.authors: Li Z, Zhang T, Wang W, Luo X, Zheng W, Han Z, Ahmad MU, Yuan Q, Chen C, Xi S, Wu L, Li W, Xie J, Feng W, Yu J, Kinahan PE, Li Z, Li G, Jiang Y.
papers.abstract: Background Peritoneal recurrence remains a common and fatal complication following curative gastric cancer surgery. Tertiary lymphoid structures are crucial indicators of immune response in cancer, and their maturation is associated with better prognosis and therapy outcomes. Evaluation of these structures could improve patient stratification for treatment of cancer but is hindered by the invasive and biased nature of histological methods. This study aimed to explore a non-invasive radiological method of assessment in patients with gastric cancer, using a novel multitask hybrid model to predict the presence and maturation status of tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence-free survival. Methods We developed CTransNet, a multitask hybrid model combining a convolutional neural network (ResNet50) and a Transformer model to predict tertiary lymphoid structure maturation and peritoneal recurrence-free survival in patients with gastric cancer. The study used retrospective data from eight Chinese cohorts of patients treated for gastric cancer at Nanfang Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, and Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (one training cohort, two internal validation cohorts, three external validation cohorts, and two independent cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 inhibitors for at least two cycles). Patients were classified into three categories based on the presence and maturation of tertiary lymphoid structures (identified using haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry staining): TLS0 (absent tertiary lymphoid structures), TLS1 (primary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures without germinal centres), and TLS2 (secondary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures with germinal centres [ie, more mature structures]). Peritoneal recurrence was assessed using imaging (ultrasonography, CT, or PET-CT), clinical signs, or reoperation. We evaluated the accuracy of the multitask hybrid model in classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Patients were stratified into risk groups using the median predicted score from the training cohort (high vs low), which was then applied to the validation cohorts. Survival outcomes (peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. We also analysed the relationships between predicted scores and responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Findings Patients in the Chinese cohorts were recruited between Jan 1, 2005, and Feb 28, 2022. In the training cohort, for classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status, values for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0·910 (95% CI 0·882-0·938) for TLS0, 0·925 (0·899-0·951) for TLS1, and 0·953 (0·933-0·974) for TLS2. For predicting peritoneal recurrence-free survival, the model achieved a concordance index of 0·654 (95% CI 0·620-0·688) in the training cohort. Across all cohorts, patients with low model scores had substantially higher 5-year peritoneal recurrence rates than those with high scores (eg, 66·69%, 95% CI 60·11-73·27 vs 26·28%, 20·05-32·51; p Interpretation By accurately predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status, peritoneal recurrence, and survival, the multitask hybrid model shows strong potential as a non-invasive tool for personalised gastric cancer care. The model's potential to identify patients who might benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy and are more likely to respond to immunotherapy could help clinicians to optimise treatment strategies. Funding None.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation remodels hepatic immune microenvironment via circadian gene dysregulation and promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
papers.authors: Yan B, Lin F, Chen L, Ke P, Wu H, Ting Chen.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) is a widespread public health issue that may adversely affect liver health. Although SD is a recognized circadian stressor, the mechanisms linking circadian rhythm-related changes to liver injury remain poorly understood. This study aims to systematically investigate the role of circadian rhythm-related genes (CRGs) in mediating SD-induced remodeling of the liver immune microenvironment and its potential implications for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) following SD. A rat SD model was used to assess hepatic injury via serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST). Functional enrichment analyses and machine learning identified pivotal CRGs. Key genes were validated across datasets and in HCC. Immune infiltration was analyzed using CIBERSORT and the Tumor Immune Estimation Resource (TIMER) database. Experimental validation in a rat SD model demonstrated significant elevations in serum ALT and AST levels, confirming the induction of hepatic injury. SD induced significant alterations in CRGs. CRGs were found to centrally regulate inflammatory, immune, and oncogenic processes. A machine learning framework identified six core CRGs ( Cirbp , Srebf1 , Fbxo31 , Hsp90aa1 , Btc , and Dlgap1 ), whose dysregulated expression was consistently validated. Furthermore, SD led to a significant reshuffling of the hepatic immune landscape, characterized by changes in five distinct immune cell types, which showed strong correlations with the six key CRGs. Notably, among the six hub CRGs, Cirbp and Hsp90aa1 were significantly associated with immune infiltration levels and prognosis in HCC patients. In addition, Serpine1 , which was independently identified by LASSO as a key SD-related gene, showed similar associations.

papers.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.
papers.authors: Yu Y, Xu C, Hua Y, Yang F, Xie S, Zhong L, Wang J, Zhang W, Wang Y, Li H, Chen K, Zhou Z, Xia S.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy, but resistance and immune-related toxicities continue to limit their benefit. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may enhance ICI efficacy and alleviate treatment-related intestinal toxicity, yet clinical responses remain inconsistent, and microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit. Moreover, clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence remains fragmented and has not been critically integrated. This review therefore evaluates the current clinical evidence for FMT in cancer immunotherapy and examines how donor-recipient interactions, microbial engraftment and function, host immunity, and tumor context jointly shape efficacy and toxicity. We organize these mechanisms within the Gut-Tumor Axis, encompassing microbial metabolites and cellular components, cross-organ immune signaling, and intratumoral microbiota. Finally, we discuss how multi-omics and computational modeling may enable more predictable and precise microbiome interventions.

papers.title: hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.
papers.authors: Shen Q, Viard M, Carrington M, Band G, Ansari MA.
papers.abstract: Motivation The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no existing tool integrates them within a unified, reproducible framework. Results We present hlafactor, a computational tool that brings together established HLA functional annotations within a single, standardised framework. Starting from two-field HLA genotype calls, whether imputed or molecularly typed, hlafactor assigns functional annotations from published reference datasets and applies established calculations to derive individual-level features. These include tapasin dependency scores, general and functional heterozygosity, allele-specific cell surface expression, NK cell-related polymorphisms (Bw4/Bw6, C1/C2, HLA-B -21 M/T), and class I/II supertype assignments. hlafactor also maps alleles to IMGT/HLA amino-acid alignments to generate residue-level genotypes. All outputs are formatted for direct use in downstream association analyses with existing software. Applied to 17,960 samples from the MalariaGEN consortium, each functional annotation module completed in under 15 seconds on a single CPU core, and preprocessing and quality control in just over four minutes, supporting its use in large cohort studies. Availability hlafactor is implemented in C ++20 and is freely available at https://github.com/QiJingS/hlafactor and archived on Zenodo under DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20647440.

papers.title: Sugar-coated bullets: Polysaccharide coated probiotics for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.authors: Xu T, Guo J, Xu H.
papers.abstract: Probiotics can alleviate inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) by regulating the gut microbiota, strengthening the intestinal barrier, and modulating intestinal immunity. However, their efficacy is severely compromised by the harsh gastrointestinal environment, including gastric acid, bile salts, and digestive enzymes. Single cell encapsulation (coated probiotics) with polysaccharides has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome this challenge. Owing to their structural diversity, tunable charge and gelation behavior, resistance to host digestive enzymes, and fermentability by the gut microbiota, polysaccharides serve as ideal coating materials that not only protect probiotics but also function synergistically as prebiotics. This review systematically summarizes the polysaccharide materials commonly used for probiotic coating, the non-covalent and covalent mechanisms underlying coating construction, and functionalization strategies including engineered bacteria, ROS-responsive systems, drug delivery, and nanoparticle loading. The therapeutic mechanisms of polysaccharide-coated probiotics in IBD were then discussed, covering three interconnected aspects: regulation of the gut microbiota, repair of the intestinal barrier, and maintenance of intestinal immune homeostasis. Current challenges and future directions toward clinical translation were also analyzed. This review aims to provide theoretical guidance for the development of next-generation polysaccharide-coated probiotics for IBD therapy.

papers.title: Profiling Histone Modifications in Harpegnathos saltator Brains by CUT&Tag.
papers.authors: Kuang M, Antonova A, Khan S, Moreno-Medina S, Bonasio R.
papers.abstract: Harpegnathos saltator ants are a powerful model for studying socially induced adult brain plasticity. In this species, adult workers can transition into reproductive gamergates, which is accompanied by extensive behavioral, physiological, and gene regulatory changes arising from a single genome. Understanding the chromatin mechanisms that regulate these transitions requires epigenomic methods that are sensitive enough to profile small organs such as insect brains. Cleavage under targets and tagmentation (CUT&Tag) is a genome-wide chromatin profiling method that can be used to map histone modifications at high resolution from low-input samples by using an antibody-directed protein A/G-Tn5 transposase to perform targeted, in situ DNA tagmentation, substantially improving the signal-to-noise ratio compared with other chromatin profiling approaches. Here, we provide a CUT&Tag protocol that has been optimized for profiling histone modifications in Harpegnathos brains. We describe the steps for nuclei isolation from insect brains, followed by antibody incubation, transposase binding and tagmentation, and library preparation for high-throughput sequencing. This protocol is further adaptable to single-cell multiomic assays, enabling high-resolution profiling of the epigenomic landscape in social insect brains and other organs.

papers.title: Apo(a) Determines Cell State and Plaque Composition in Advanced Atherosclerotic Lesions in Mice.
papers.authors: Assini JM, Pang S, Chuecos MA, Lagor WR, Andrews T, Boffa MB, Koschinsky ML.
papers.abstract: Elevated Lp(a) (lipoprotein[a]) is an independent and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and patients with high Lp(a) demonstrate more severe plaque pathology. However, the mechanism driving the impact of Lp(a) on atherogenesis in vivo remains unclear. We generated transgenic mice expressing human apo(a) (LPA), which forms a noncovalent complex with mouse apo B100, and compared them to wild-type mice. After 6 or 24 weeks of a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet and hepatic Ldlr knockdown, atherosclerotic lesion composition by histopathologic staining and immunofluorescence imaging was assessed. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of 24-week lesions was performed to identify the cell types within the atherosclerotic plaque, differentially expressed genes, and biological pathways affected by the LPA transgene. High apo(a) levels in both sexes of LPA mice significantly increased lesion area in the aortic sinus compared with wild-type controls after 24 weeks of feeding. LPA mice demonstrated more severe atherosclerosis features, such as increased necrotic area and oxidized phospholipid deposition, increased calcification, and disorganized collagen accumulation in a thinner fibrous cap. Our single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis revealed that the greatest transcriptomic effects in LPA mice occurred in resident-like macrophages, whereby gene signatures associated with smooth muscle cell differentiation, extracellular matrix/actin organization, and TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta) signaling were upregulated and immune-response/chemokine signaling programs were downregulated. Reclustering of resident-like macrophages revealed a subpopulation that, in addition to myeloid markers, expresses mesenchymal/stromal-associated genes; RNA velocity analysis revealed that these cells were in a transitionary cell state, resembling a more mesenchymal phenotype compared with classically defined resident-like macrophages. This differentiation phenomenon is known as macrophage to mesenchymal/myofibroblast transition. Moreover, we found increased abundance of transitionary macrophage to mesenchymal/myofibroblast transition cells within lesions from LPA mice compared with wild-type mice. Our data establish a novel role for apo(a) in macrophage to mesenchymal/myofibroblast transition as a possible contributor to the proatherosclerotic effects of Lp(a).

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Sheikh MR, Parvez MAS, Tasnim J, Alam Muhib MM, Ahmed MT, Nandi P, Ali SME, Chakraborty A, Iqbal A, Uddin ME.
papers.abstract: Background Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized. Objectives This study aimed to systematically identify and characterize potential molecular targets of curcumin and resveratrol in LUAD using an integrated computational framework. Methods Potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol were collected from multiple compound-target databases and integrated with LUAD-associated genes obtained from GeneCards and OMIM. Shared targets were evaluated using protein-protein interaction analysis and network-based prioritization. Transcriptomic and clinical validation was performed using The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-LUAD dataset, including differential expression, diagnostic performance, survival analysis, mutation profiling, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune association, immune checkpoint correlation, and co-expression analysis. Structurally prioritized targets were subsequently investigated using molecular docking, interaction profiling, and redocking validation, followed by molecular dynamics and binding free energy analyses. Results The integrated target-screening strategy identified 976 unique targets for curcumin, 6,897 targets for resveratrol, and 3,885 LUAD-associated targets, with 325 common targets between curcumin, resveratrol, and LUAD. Downstream investigation of potential targets identified MMP1 and MMP9 from network and multi-level evidence prioritization. Both genes demonstrated diagnostic potential in TCGA-LUAD, with MMP1 achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9281 (95% CI: 0.8785-0.9776) and MMP9 an AUC of 0.8466 (95% CI: 0.7727-0.9205). However, MMP1 and MMP9 were not independently related to overall survival in stage-adjusted survival analysis models. Functional enrichment analysis identified biological pathways associated with the expression profiles of MMP1 and MMP9, while immune cells, immune checkpoint, and gene co-expression analyses indicated broader molecular and immune associations. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable predicted binding of curcumin and resveratrol to MMP1 and MMP9, with docking scores ranging from -7.0 to -9.9 kcal/mol. Mutation analysis further identified an MMP1 p.R214S variant at a residue corresponding to ARG214 involved in the predicted resveratrol interaction, suggesting a potentially relevant structural association. Molecular dynamics and MM/GBSA analysis showed that the selected complexes are stable and energetically favorable. DFT calculation indicated different electronic properties of both the compounds, ADMET analysis demonstrated good drug like properties for both compounds, complying the Lipinski's Rule of Five. Conclusion Overall, this integrated computational analysis identified MMP1, and MMP9 as potential molecular targets associated with curcumin and resveratrol in LUAD. The combined structural, dynamic, electronic, pharmacokinetic, and toxicity evaluations provide a comprehensive framework for prioritizing these compounds and targets for further experimental investigation.

papers.title: Mechanisms of action and evolutionary relationships of phage anti-defence proteins.
papers.authors: Murtazalieva K, Karatzas E, Yang ALJ, Corona F, Wang J, Typas A, Finn RD.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages and bacteria are engaged in a perpetual molecular arms race, in which phage anti-defence proteins (ADPs) enable phages to evade bacterial immune systems. Although numerous novel ADPs have recently been discovered, the mechanisms by which most act remain uncharacterised. Here, we employed computational structural approaches to predict mechanisms of action for 19 uncharacterised ADPs. Many ADPs, while inhibiting one defence system, simultaneously trigger another, and we found features shared by these proteins, and in addition revealed previously unreported links between ADPs and defence triggers. Given the extensive evolutionary links between bacterial and eukaryotic viruses, and the established homology between eukaryotic innate immune systems and bacterial defences, we hypothesised that eukaryotic viruses may encode homologues of phage ADPs and use them to evade eukaryotic immunity. We identified homologues for 20 phage ADPs in eukaryotic viruses, with nucleotidyltransferase predicted to retain analogous functions. Together, these findings shed light on the putative mechanistic diversity of phage ADPs and suggest that molecular strategies for immune evasion may be conserved across the prokaryotic and eukaryotic viruses.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics-Driven Discovery of the Novel Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR)-T Cell Targets Erb-B2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinase 3 (ErbB3) and Solute Carrier Family 1 Member 5 (SLC1A5) in Melanoma.
papers.authors: Juraschek KF, Güse E, Hof MMC, Lischer C, Feuchter N, Schuler-Thurner B, Koch EAT, Jager MJ, Biburger M, Berking C, Dörrie J, Vera J, Schaft N.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has shown limited success in solid tumors, mainly because of the scarcity of tumor-specific surface antigens. To address this challenge, we developed an integrated computational and experimental pipeline for antigen discovery and applied it to melanoma. Our bioinformatics strategy introduced a novel quantitative metric, the restrictiveness ratio , to identify antigens highly expressed in tumors but minimally present in healthy tissues. Using RNA-sequencing data from patient samples, we compared candidate targets with the established melanoma antigen chondroitin sulphate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4) and validated their expression on melanoma cell lines. CARs were engineered against selected antigens, CAR-T cells were generated by RNA electroporation, and expression was confirmed. Functional validation included T cell activation, cytokine secretion, and cytotoxicity assays. RNA-seq analysis of cutaneous and uveal melanoma identified 90 and 84 candidate genes, respectively, encoding transmembrane proteins with tumor expression above 10 TPM (transcripts per million). Fifty-six genes displayed higher restrictiveness ratios than CSPG4. Following manual curation and scFv (single-chain variable fragment) availability assessment, five candidates were prioritized. CARs targeting ErbB3 and SLC1A5 induced strong antigen-specific T cell activation and cytotoxicity comparable to CSPG4-CARs. These findings identify ErbB3 and SLC1A5 as promising CAR-T targets and establish an integrative bioinformatics-driven framework for extending CAR-T therapy to solid tumors.

papers.title: Single-Cell Profiling Reveals Coordinated Epithelial and Microenvironmental Remodeling in Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Resistant Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhu L, Shen Y, Yang F, Wang F, Bao M, Lin J, Chen J, Hu Q.
papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors remains a major challenge in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma, yet the cellular states and microenvironmental alterations associated with resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed a single-cell transcriptomic analysis of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma samples to characterize resistance-associated cellular heterogeneity and intercellular communication. We identified substantial transcriptional and compositional heterogeneity across epithelial, immune, and stromal compartments. Secondary analysis of epithelial cells identified a resistance-enriched epithelial state with relatively elevated inferred copy-number variation and a distinct transcriptional profile. Single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering analysis identified cluster-associated regulon patterns involving ZFP90, FOSL2, NFYB, NFE2L1, SMAD1, and ETV7; however, sample-level differences in ETV7, FOSL2, and SMAD1 activity between this state and the remaining epithelial subclusters were not statistically significant. CellChat inferred a higher aggregate communication strength in the resistant group and predicted interactions between the resistance-associated epithelial state and multiple immune and stromal populations, including MIF and extracellular-matrix-associated signaling. Integration of transcriptional regulatory and intercellular communication analyses further connected epithelial regulatory programs with microenvironmental signaling. Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction supported representative resistance-associated transcriptional alterations identified by the single-cell analyses. Collectively, our findings characterize a resistance-associated epithelial state and its predicted regulatory and intercellular communication patterns, providing a descriptive framework for investigating the resistant tumor ecosystem.

papers.title: A multi-epitope vaccine based on AdeK, PirA, and Omp22 elicits specific antibodies binding to Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.authors: Wang H, Ji X, Ju L, Han H, Mao L.
papers.abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) has classified Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) as a critical-priority pathogen that requires novel antibiotics and strategies, due to its high antibiotic resistance. To combat the critical public health threat posed by CRAB, bioinformatics and immunoinformatic tools were used in this study to predict potential linear B lymphocyte (LBL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes derived from the Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) outer membrane proteins AdeK, PirA, and outer membrane protein 22 (Omp22). Subsequently, four combined multi-epitope vaccines (MEVs) designated ABV1-ABV4 were constructed by linking selected LBL, HTL, and CTL epitopes and Pan-HLA-DR reactive epitopes (PADRE) via GGGS and AAY linkers and fusing four different adjuvants to the N-terminus of the constructs with EAAAK linkers to increase immunogenicity. Afterward, the allergenicity, antigenicity, and solubility of ABV1-ABV4 were analyzed. The two non-allergenic candidates ABV3 and ABV4 were further analyzed for physicochemical properties and immune simulation using ExPASy ProtParam and C-ImmSim. ABV4 exhibited superior antigenicity and solubility compared with ABV3, and both ABV4 and ABV3 were predicted to induce similar immune responses; therefore, ABV4 was selected for further structural characterization and subsequent expression. The 3D structure was modeled using AlphaFold 3.0 and refined with GalaxyRefine servers. After refinement, the quality of the 3D structure improved markedly, with 97.2% of the residues in the most favored regions of the Ramachandran plot and an overall Z score of -6.11. Docking scores were -274.02 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR2 and -302.54 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR4. MM/PBSA calculations yielded binding free energies of -53.66 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR2 and -68.93 kcal/mol for ABV4-TLR4. The optimized ABV4 gene was synthesized, cloned and inserted into pET28a, and expressed in E. coli BL21 with a C-terminal 6 × His tag. Immunization of mice with ABV4 induced high titers of anti-ABV4 antibodies and elevated serum IFN-γ and IL-4 levels, suggesting that ABV4 may elicit both humoral and cellular immune responses in mice. Immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) revealed that the ABV4 antibody specifically recognized CRAB extracellular proteins without cross-reactivity to E. coli, K. pneumoniae, or P. aeruginosa, confirming that ABV4 is a promising MEV vaccine candidate against CRAB with the potential to induce humoral and cellular immune responses. Overall, ABV4 is a promising vaccine candidate against CRAB, and further experimental research is required to validate the protective efficacy in mice and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Transcriptional Landscape of Immune Cells and Key Gene Expression in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Approach.
papers.authors: Weng G, Ying W, Miao Z, Zhang Q, Chen P.
papers.abstract: Background Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a common malignancy with considerable heterogeneity and complex interactions within the tumor microenvironment. Information about the transcriptional heterogeneity of immune cells and expression profiles of important genes can shed light on disease progression and identify potential therapeutic targets. Methods We employed single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize the immune cell landscape in ESCC. We analyzed cellular composition and transcriptional heterogeneity using dimensionality reduction methodologies including UMAP and t-SNE. To further identify active biological processes and signaling pathways in the immune microenvironment, we determined Gene Ontology (GO) and pathway enrichment. Results We identified a complex structure of immune cell subpopulations, demonstrating distinct transcriptional patterns. Specific expression patterns of some key genes were evident among the cell types, including high expression in regulatory T cells and natural killer T cells. The SPP1 signaling pathway emerged as a potentially important candidate in computationally inferred immune cell communication. Pseudotime analysis showed dynamic changes in representative gene expression, indicating transcriptional state variation. Conclusion The complex immune response in the ESCC microenvironment is revealed in this study through the exploration of immune cells and key gene activity at single-cell transcriptional resolution. This knowledge may help guide the development of personalized immunotherapies by revealing the roles of specific immune cells and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Aging-Related Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Immune Heterogeneity in Tuberculosis: An Exploratory Multi-Cohort Analysis.
papers.authors: Xu A, Reyimu A, Maimaiti M, Gao F, Kamili G, Zou X, He C.
papers.abstract: Background Aging-related genes (ARGs) may contribute to immune heterogeneity in tuberculosis (TB), but their diagnostic and biological relevance remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify TB-associated ARG transcripts, characterize their immune and molecular correlates, and evaluate their exploratory diagnostic performance across prespecified cohorts. Patients and methods Public TB transcriptomic cohorts were analyzed together with a local bulk RNA-seq cohort comprising 5 TB patients and 5 controls and a local single-cell RNA-seq cohort comprising 3 active TB patients and 3 controls. The local cohorts were selected using random sampling. Age-adjusted differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, immune-infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, single-cell annotation, and Comparative Toxicogenomics Database-based compound-gene screening were performed. Results GSE83456 included 45 TB patients and 61 controls. Age-adjusted differential expression identified 189 differentially expressed genes, and the intersection of DEGs, ARGs, and blue-module genes yielded 11 discovery candidates. Nested model selection in GSE83456 identified a naive Bayes classifier based on STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14. Across five repeated stratified nested cross-validation runs, the mean AUC was 0.962, with a repeat-level range of 0.954-0.969. Balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 0.926, 0.911, 0.941, and 0.928, respectively. Exploratory evaluations included GSE19439, GSE34608, GSE62525, GSE19444, and the local RNA-seq cohort. Consensus clustering separated TB samples into two ARG-associated subgroups with distinct immune-infiltration and pathway-activity profiles. CIBERSORT analysis identified significant TB-control differences in 9 of 22 inferred immune-cell types. Single-cell analysis demonstrated heterogeneous expression of STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14 across annotated immune-cell subsets. CTD screening generated exploratory compound-gene associations that provide testable hypotheses for future experimental studies. Conclusion Age-adjusted multi-cohort analysis identified candidate ARG-associated TB markers and immune patterns. STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14 are candidate markers rather than clinically validated biomarkers and require independent experimental and clinical validation.

papers.title: Primary Dermal Modeling of Hypersensitivity Reactions for Allergen Identification.
papers.authors: Bridgewater HA, Shaia C, Long CM.
papers.abstract: Whole cell vaccines (WCVs) against Coxiella burnetii, the causative agent of Q fever, are effective and long-lasting; however, pre-exposed individuals can experience a post-vaccination hypersensitivity (PVH) response to WCVs. In this study, an ex vivo human skin model is used to investigate the mechanisms behind early immune events during the sensitization phase of the PVH response following C. burnetii inactivated whole-cell vaccination. The ex vivo human skin model is injected intradermally with a saline negative control, two strains of inactivated WCVs, and an E. coli LPS inflammatory positive control. The culture media and gel matrix can be processed for cytokine analysis. The skin tissue can be separated from the adipose and formalin-fixed for histopathology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and/or spatial biology. Additionally, fixed single-cell suspensions can be used for single-cell RNA sequencing. Representative data from this model demonstrate that IL-6 levels are significantly increased in whole-cell vaccine and LPS-injected cultures. Further, macrophages can be identified using both IHC and spatial biology. Transcriptional analysis is enabled by single-cell suspension viabilities ranging from 19% to 32%, which is adequate for single-cell RNA sequencing analysis. This protocol enables a deeper understanding of the initial immune response to C. burnetii WCVs, with the goal of understanding mechanisms of PVH sensitization.

papers.title: Hidden PI3K-Akt gene programs define stromal, immune, and spatial contexts associated with ovarian cancer prognosis and chemotherapy response.
papers.authors: Li Y, Liu Z.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated PI3K-Akt signaling contributes to ovarian cancer progression and treatment resistance, but its effects occur within a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment. We investigated whether clinically relevant PI3K-Akt programs include hidden network-dependent signals associated with prognosis and chemotherapy response. We analyzed 327 PI3K-Akt pathway genes in TCGA ovarian cancer using netLDA to identify outcome-associated programs containing marginal and network-supported hidden signals. Prognostic performance was evaluated in independent cohorts. Predictive regulatory modules (PRMs) were characterized using protein-protein interactions, pathway and tumor-microenvironment analyses, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, spatial transcriptomics, and model-based virtual perturbation. We identified a 50-gene signature comprising 18 marginal-effect genes and 32 hidden network-supported genes, with 38 genes organized into five PRMs centered on HSP90AB1, EFNA2, LAMC1, GNG12, and EPHA2 and the remaining 12 retained as singleton features. The modules represented distinct stress/survival, receptor, ECM/stromal, inflammatory/immune, and cell-matrix adhesion programs and showed prognostic value across independent cohorts. LAMC1-PRM was associated with stromal and EMT features and localized to fibroblast/CAF-rich contexts, whereas GNG12-PRM was associated with immune signaling and myeloid compartments. Spatial transcriptomics revealed nonrandom organization and response-associated differences, including stronger LAMC1-fibroblast/CAF organization in poor-response tissues and increasing GNG12-myeloid organization with response. Virtual perturbation supported network-dependent predictive contributions not evident from marginal effects alone. Clinically relevant PI3K-Akt dysregulation comprises biologically distinct network-dependent programs spanning tumor, stromal, immune, and spatial compartments. Contrasting LAMC1-centered stromal/ECM and GNG12-centered immune/myeloid organizations were associated with chemotherapy-response heterogeneity, linking hidden PI3K-Akt signals to ovarian tumor microenvironment architecture.

papers.title: Residual gastric cancer risk after Helicobacter pylori eradication: Mucosal immune trajectories (Review).
papers.authors: Chen J, Tang B, Zhou L.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori is the leading modifiable cause of noncardia gastric cancer. Eradication lowers the incidence of primary and metachronous gastric neoplasia, yet a clinically meaningful risk remains once extensive atrophy, intestinal metaplasia or dysplasia is established. Current surveillance incorporates infection status and structural disease burden but does not directly assess biological recovery of the gastric mucosa. The present review examined whether mucosal immune trajectories after eradication are heterogeneous and whether localized immune measurements could explain variation in residual risk beyond morphology and epithelial-field alterations. Single-cell and spatial studies of human tissue have identified infection- and precursor-associated changes in myeloid differentiation, antigen presentation, T-cell states, metaplastic epithelium and stroma. Longitudinal evidence is less developed. Selected mucosal T-cell measurements support reversibility of specific responses, whereas gene-expression, histologic and microbiome trajectories provide molecular, structural or contextual evidence. Outcome-linked CD8-associated trajectories provide the closest currently available clinical-outcome immune evidence, but remain non-functional proxies derived from a post-resection population. A 2026 human single-cell study further identified persistent stromal and immunosuppressive niche features in post-eradication chronic atrophic gastritis, but did not provide paired longitudinal immune-function measurements or prospective neoplastic outcomes. Among the studies identified through the present search, none combined confirmation of eradication, paired measurements of immune function, concurrent assessment of the epithelial field and prospective dysplasia or cancer outcomes in individuals without previous gastric neoplasia. Therefore, the available evidence supports heterogeneous tissue recovery rather than a validated persistent immune state. Clinical translation would require reproducible functional immune activity, or a functionally validated proxy, together with independent outcome association, external validation and a clinically meaningful improvement in surveillance decisions beyond established histologic staging and lesion extent. Until such evidence is available, candidate immune markers should remain research tools and should not modify guideline-based surveillance.

papers.title: Finerenone attenuates experimental autoimmune myocarditis and modulates cardiac macrophage and Th17-cell responses.
papers.authors: Du P, Zhao Y, Su R, Hu K, Bai L, Cui X, Sun Z, Yang Y, Wei X, Jiao B, Guan S, Han D, Lu Y, Zhang J, Tang J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Autoimmune myocarditis is characterized by immune-mediated myocardial injury and remodeling. However, whether the selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist finerenone modulates the cardiac cellular microenvironment in autoimmune myocarditis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of finerenone on experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM) and its regulation of the cardiac cellular microenvironment. Methods An EAM model was established in BALB/c mice by α -myosin heavy chain immunization, followed by finerenone treatment. Echocardiography, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and RT-qPCR were used to evaluate cardiac injury, inflammation, fibrosis, and function. Single-cell RNA sequencing, T-cell receptor clonotype analysis, transcription factor regulatory network analysis, and cell-cell communication analysis were performed to characterize finerenone-induced changes in cardiac immune and stromal cell populations. Flow cytometry and macrophage-CD4 + T-cell co-culture experiments were performed to further validate the immune-related findings. Results Finerenone alleviated myocardial injury, inflammatory infiltration, and collagen deposition and improved left ventricular systolic function in EAM mice, including under a delayed-treatment regimen.
