Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that finerenone remodeled the cardiac cellular microenvironment, reduced remodeling-associated Spp1 + macrophages and inflammation-associated Cxcl10 + macrophages, and suppressed IRF7-, STAT1-, STAT2-, and RFX5-associated transcriptional programs. Finerenone also reduced Th17-related inflammatory and cytotoxic programs and T-cell clonal expansion. Cell-cell communication analysis predicted reduced macrophage-Th17-cell communication, particularly MHC-II-associated signaling. Furthermore, macrophage-CD4 + T-cell co-cultures from finerenone-treated EAM mice exhibited reduced CD4 + T-cell proliferation and IL-17A + CD4 + T-cell proportions compared with those from untreated EAM mice. Profibrotic fibroblast programs and neutrophil inflammatory signaling were also suppressed. Discussion Targeting mineralocorticoid receptor-related immune networks may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for autoimmune myocarditis.

papers.title: Sequencing based dissection of inflammation associated natural killer cell remodeling in lung adenocarcinoma identifies state biomarkers and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
papers.authors: Chang L, Wang R, Chen X, Fang Y, Yan J, Chen J, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic inflammation may shift tissue-protective immunity toward a tumor-permissive microenvironment, but natural killer (NK)-cell remodeling in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains incompletely characterized. We investigated whether NK-cell depletion and state redistribution are reproducible tumor-associated features with biomarker or therapeutic relevance. Methods Two patient-matched single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts (GSE131907 and E-MTAB-13526) were analyzed using patient-level paired tests. We assessed NK-cell abundance within the immune compartment, CD16-positive terminal and CD16-negative tissue-adapted fractions within NK cells, and pseudobulk expression. Chromatin accessibility was evaluated using GSE304741 GEX-ATAC data. TCGA-LUAD, Visium spatial transcriptomics, and six pretreatment immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cohorts provided external assessment. Western blots in NK-92 cells examined SMAD2 phosphorylation and perforin/granzyme B expression after TGF-β1 stimulation with or without SB431542. Results In GSE131907, NK-cell abundance and terminal-state fractions declined in all 10 matched patients, whereas tissue-adapted fractions increased (all P = 0.00293); these patterns were independently replicated. Pseudobulk effects showed moderate genome-wide concordance (Spearman's ρ = 0.350), with 112/116 discovery-significant genes directionally concordant and 58 significant in both cohorts (FDR Conclusion LUAD exhibits reproducible NK-cell depletion accompanied by loss of terminal-state representation and relative enrichment of tissue-adapted states. Terminal cytotoxic programs and abundance-adjusted state balance warrant investigation as biopsy-based biomarkers, whereas KLRC1/NKG2A and TGF-β-hypoxia signaling remain therapeutic hypotheses requiring further validation. These findings do not establish a longitudinal premalignant trajectory.

papers.title: Macrophage state in neoadjuvant and perioperative immunotherapy resistance in resectable NSCLC: a critical appraisal of strategies from CSF1R and CD47-SIRPα to CAR-macrophages.
papers.authors: Li H, Li B, Li Z, Wang Z, Sun W, Yang K, Yang Y, Wang B.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant or perioperative chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard treatment option for selected patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with eligibility determined by tumor stage, nodal involvement, oncogenic-driver status, regimen, and jurisdiction. Even so, most patients do not achieve a pathological complete response, and the determinants of resistance in early-stage disease remain incompletely understood. Tumor-associated macrophages are a key, and targetable, component of that resistance. We argue that abundance alone is an insufficient predictor of whether the myeloid compartment supports or suppresses a checkpoint-dependent response, and that macrophage state, namely the dominant subset, its spatial niche, and its trajectory under therapy, adds explanatory and therapeutic information whose weight remains to be established. Single-cell and spatial studies have identified metabolically distinct SPP1 + , CCL18 + , and oncofetal STAB1 + states associated with immunosuppressive niches in NSCLC, although these labels vary between datasets and their functional assignments are provisional. Limited serial neoadjuvant data from a single cohort suggest that treatment expands tissue-resident macrophages and shifts tumor-associated macrophages toward a neutral rather than antitumor phenotype, most evidently in tumors that reached a major pathological response. Current agents, including CSF1R and CD47-SIRPα blockade, TREM2, LILRB2 and PI3Kγ inhibitors, and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) macrophages, act on programs that cut across these subsets rather than on the subsets themselves, and almost all efficacy evidence derives from advanced or preclinical disease. The resectable, biomarker-rich perioperative window is nonetheless the most informative setting in which to test subset-informed myeloid reprogramming.

papers.title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
papers.authors: Li K, Ye X, Wang H, Liang L, Zeng R, Zhou Z, Huang Z, Chen Z, Liang H, Du H, Shang Z, Ma M, Yang L, Zhou Y.
papers.abstract: Background Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms. Methods Bulk RNA-seq datasets were combined to perform differential expression profiling, ferroptosis evaluation, weighted co-expression network construction, functional pathway annotation, and machine-learning-driven feature screening. Subsequently, single-cell transcriptomic data were examined to map the cell-type-specific localization of the hub genes that had been pinpointed. Natural product and compound-target databases were subsequently searched for small-molecule compounds associated with both AS and the key target. Candidate compounds were subjected to batch molecular docking. Based on its predicted binding properties and biological relevance, Ursolic acid (UA) was selected as a candidate drug. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the stability of the UA-PPARγ complex. The therapeutic effects of UA were subsequently examined in an AS mouse model and in BMP-2/4-induced osteogenic differentiation of fibroblasts. Histological staining, qRT-PCR, and western blotting were used to assess inflammatory responses, pathological osteogenesis, and PPARγ-related signaling. Results Integrated transcriptomic analysis identified 20 genes shared among AS-related differentially expressed genes, ferroptosis-related genes, and genes from ferroptosis-associated co-expression modules. Machine-learning analysis further identified PHF21A, PPARG , and TP53INP1 as hub genes, among which PPARG showed the highest predictive contribution and distinct expression patterns across immune cell populations. Database-based natural product screening and batch molecular docking identified UA as a promising PPARγ-targeting candidate. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported a potential interaction between UA and PPARγ. In vivo , UA markedly alleviated inflammatory infiltration, reduced the expression of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-17, and attenuated pathological bone formation in AS mice. In vitro , UA increased PPARγ expression while suppressing the osteogenic markers COL1A1, ALP, RUNX2, OPN, and BMP-2, thereby inhibiting the osteogenic transdifferentiation of fibroblasts. Conclusion This study established an integrated strategy combining ferroptosis-related bioinformatics analysis, machine-learning-based target identification, natural product screening, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. PPARγ was identified as a ferroptosis-associated molecular target in AS, and UA exerted concurrent anti-inflammatory and anti-osteogenic effects accompanied by increased PPARγ protein expression. These findings suggest that targeting PPARγ with UA might be a potential therapeutic strategy for AS.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Identification of metabolism-associated biomarkers with a focus on ketone body pathways in diabetic retinopathy by integrating transcriptomics and single-cell analysis.
papers.authors: Cheng Q, Qu Y, Chen M, Qin L, Li J, Hu Y.
papers.abstract: Background To identify potential biomarkers of ketone body metabolism (KBM) associated with diabetic retinopathy (DR), and to explore possible underlying mechanism between KBM and DR. Methods Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between DR and healthy normal control (NC) samples were acquired in GSE221521.Then, DEGs and KBM-related genes (KBM-RGs) were interleaved to discern candidate genes, and the key feature genes were derived through two algorithms of machine learning. Next, biomarkers were generated through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves analysis and expression validation in GSE221521 and GSE189005.Then, enrichment analysis, immune infiltration and single-cell RNA sequencing analysis were conducted.Finally, experimental validation of biomarkers was conducted through reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Results ACACA and WDTC1 were recognized as DR-associated candidate biomarkers. ACACA was enriched in Reactome RNA polymerase II transcription pathway, and WDTC1 was enriched in Reactome eukaryotic translation initiation pathway. Two types of immune cells, namely activated NK cells and monocytes, were significantly different between DR and NC samples in bulk immune infiltration analysis. Next, NK cells and T cells were identified as key cell types based on cell proportion analysis. Both ACACA and WDTC1 were highly expressed in NK cells and T cells. Cell-cell communication patterns changed in the DR group. ACACA and WDTC1 showed stable expression during the differentiation of T cells and NK cells. Finally, RT-qPCR results showed that ACACA and WDTC1 were up-regulated in DR samples. This concurred with the results yielded by bioinformatics analysis. Conclusion This study identified two metabolism-associated biomarkers (ACACA and WDTC1) that may serve as DR-associated candidate biomarkers. These preliminary findings suggest potential molecular leads for further investigation, though prospective validation in larger cohorts is needed.

papers.title: Multi-source analysis identifies an NPC2-associated macrophage transcriptional program in ulcerative colitis.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Yang W, Wang K, Guo Q.
papers.abstract: Background Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves extensive remodeling of intestinal macrophage states, but the molecular programs linking inflammation, lysosomal function, and lipid handling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify macrophage-associated molecules and cellular states linked to UC. Methods We integrated UC single-cell RNA sequencing, bone marrow-derived macrophage polarization transcriptomes, UK Biobank OLINK proteomic associations, external bulk transcriptomic datasets, and spatial transcriptomics. Candidate molecules were further examined in dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis and macrophage activation models. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, receiver operating characteristic, and Spearman correlation analyses were performed as appropriate. Results Twelve genes were shared among UC-associated macrophage differentially expressed genes, macrophage polarization-related genes, and UC-associated circulating protein signals. NPC2 was prioritized based on its macrophage enrichment, external transcriptomic performance, and established lysosomal function. Single-cell reclustering identified an NPC2+MMP12+ macrophage subset with heterogeneous abundance across donors. Donor-level analysis showed a numerically higher median proportion of NPC2+MMP12+ macrophages in UC than in controls, but the difference was not statistically significant (17.7% vs. 9.3%; two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, P = 0.471). NPC2-high macrophages exhibited enrichment of lysosomal, phagocytic, complement, lipid-handling, antigen-presentation, and tissue-remodeling programs. Spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed a positive association between NPC2 expression and macrophage-related signatures in inflamed mucosal regions. NPC2 expression was also increased in DSS-induced colitis and inflammatory macrophage models. Cholesteryl sulfate sodium (CSS) reduced nitrite production and shifted macrophage marker expression away from CD86 predominance, although NPC2 dependence was not established. Conclusions NPC2 is associated with a lysosome-related macrophage transcriptional program observed in UC. These exploratory findings support further investigation of macrophage lysosomal lipid handling and warrant functional and independent clinical validation.

papers.title: STING signaling opposes AXL to regulate interferon responses in dedifferentiated human melanoma.
papers.authors: Shirley CA, Wolfe MB, Anaya-Aldrete KB, Nihal M, Chhabra G, McIlwain SJ, Krien JM, Ndiaye MA, Ahmad N.
papers.abstract: Introduction Cancer cells can evade interferon (IFN) signaling pressures by suppressing intrinsic innate immune signaling pathways or dedifferentiating, giving rise to immunotherapy-resistant cell states. Therapeutic strategies specifically tailored to account for and eliminate such states remain limited. Methods Here, we genetically reintroduced stimulator of interferon genes (STING) in dedifferentiated STING-deficient melanoma cells, used AXL receptor tyrosine kinase (AXL) small-molecule inhibition, and analyzed publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets to examine connections between dedifferentiation and interferon responses in human melanoma. Results We found that STING reintroduction induced type I IFN signaling, increased expression of antigen-presentation genes, and enhanced sensitivity to exogenous type II IFN. STING signaling silenced expression of AXL, a key marker of melanoma dedifferentiation. AXL small-molecule inhibition partially phenocopied STING reintroduction, potentiating antigen-presentation gene expression and enhancing type II IFN sensitivity in dedifferentiated human melanoma cells. Consistently, analysis of publicly available human melanoma scRNA-Seq data revealed tumor cells with concomitant STING loss and AXL gain are positively enriched for melanocyte stem-cell-like signatures, while negatively enriched for interferon and immune activation signatures. Discussion Together, through manipulation of human melanoma cell lines and analysis of single-cell states, our results support opposing roles for STING and AXL in the regulation of antigen-presenting genes and interferon sensitivity and more broadly implicate changes to interferon sensitivity in the dedifferentiation process.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies mitochondria-related biomarkers for Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis with validation in mouse and human bone tissues.
papers.authors: Deng X, Yang F, Li J, Peng J, Peng C, Yang L, Qian H, Ao J.
papers.abstract: Background Staphylococcus aureus (SA)-induced osteomyelitis (OM) is a severe orthopedic infection characterized by complex host-pathogen interactions and limited molecular markers for lesion assessment. Mitochondrial dysfunction is closely linked to infection-induced inflammatory and metabolic remodeling, but mitochondria-related signatures in SA-induced OM remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify mitochondria-related candidate biomarkers for SA-induced OM and evaluate their associations with immune infiltration and regulated cell death. Methods Peripheral-blood transcriptomic datasets GSE16129 and GSE6269 were used as the training cohort, and whole-blood dataset GSE30119 was used as an external evaluation cohort. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using limma and intersected with MitoCarta3.0 to obtain mitochondria-related DEGs (MRDEGs). GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed. Core MRDEGs were selected using LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Random Forest, and diagnostic models were trained and evaluated using eight machine-learning algorithms. Immune infiltration was assessed by CIBERSORT, and cell death-related pathway activity was analyzed using ssGSEA. The expression of core MRDEGs was further validated in a SA-induced OM mouse model by RT-qPCR and Western blotting, and in human bone tissue specimens by Western blotting. Results Twenty MRDEGs were identified, and five core genes, QTRT1, ABCB6, PPIF, ACSL1, and GLRX5, were selected. The LASSO-based model showed the best performance in the external evaluation cohort, with an AUC of 0.879. These genes were associated with neutrophil, macrophage, and monocyte infiltration, as well as cell death-related pathways, including ferroptosis, apoptosis, and NETosis. Mouse and human bone tissue validation further supported disease-associated expression changes of the five core genes. Conclusion This study identifies a mitochondria-related five-gene signature associated with SA-induced OM. These genes may serve as tissue-based adjunctive molecular indicators for SA-induced OM lesion assessment and provide a framework for linking mitochondrial dysfunction, immune remodeling, and regulated cell death in osteomyelitis.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

papers.title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma.
papers.authors: Lin K, Cui Y, Jiang Y, Zheng M, Yang Y, Chen J, Wu W, Xu N.
papers.abstract: Purpose Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression. Methods RNA-sequencing and clinical data from 80 UM patients were obtained from TCGA. Thirty highly connected hypoxia-related genes were prioritized through protein-protein interaction analysis and evaluated using five complementary survival-based machine learning approaches: LASSO-Cox, CoxBoost, random survival forest, XGBoost-Cox, and Survival-SVM. Genes supported by at least three of the five methods were defined as core candidates and further evaluated by multivariable Cox regression to construct the prognostic model. The prognostic relevance of the model was evaluated in the dependent GSE22138 cohort using metastasis-free survival (MFS) as the clinical endpoint. Survival analysis, ROC, PCA, GSEA, and immune microenvironment analyses were performed. PFKP was further examined for its associations with immune features and experimentally validated through in vitro and in vivo assays. Results Multi-algorithm consensus identified PFKP, ENO3, and FOXO3 as core candidate genes. PFKP showed the strongest cross-model consistency and was supported by all five methods, whereas ENO3 and FOXO3 were supported by four methods. Multivariable Cox regression retained ENO3 and PFKP as the final prognostic genes, yielding a parsimonious two-gene risk model that was further evaluated in the independent GSE22138 cohort. Higher risk scores were associated with worse overall survival in TCGA-UM, shorter MFS in GSE22138, and more advanced disease. Hypoxia- and glycolysis-related pathways were enriched in the high-risk group, which also exhibited higher immune and stromal scores, lower tumor purity, and increased expression of immune checkpoint genes. PFKP expression was positively associated with CD8 + T-cell infiltration and immune checkpoint-related gene expression. Functionally, PFKP knockdown reduced UM cell proliferation, migration, and glycolytic activity in vitro and suppressed xenograft tumor growth in vivo . Conclusion We established a cross-algorithm hypoxia-related prognostic framework for UM. ENO3 and PFKP constituted the final prognostic signature, while PFKP, supported by all five algorithms and experimental validation, emerged as a functionally relevant glycolysis-related candidate associated with UM progression.

papers.title: Plasma LCP1-HRG contrast and sepsis mortality: LCP1 knockdown attenuates inflammasome-associated lytic responses in THP-1 cells.
papers.authors: Pan F, Wang Q, Jin H, Tong H, Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Background Lymphocyte cytosolic protein 1 (LCP1; L-plastin) and histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) represent distinct aspects of immune-cell biology and circulating protein homeostasis. We examined whether a standardized contrast between these proteins was associated with sepsis mortality and investigated the effect of intracellular LCP1 knockdown on inflammasome-associated injury in THP-1 cells. Methods Exploratory plasma-proteomic screening in PXD051271 and PXD055932 informed selection of LCP1 and HRG. An equal-weight contrast, z [z (LCP1) - z (HRG)], was evaluated in the PXD051271 train, test, validation, and auxiliary HERO populations and in the separate PXD055932 source study. Logistic models estimated 30-day mortality associations, and five-fold cross-validation within each population assessed incremental discrimination. Paired day-1/day-4 plasma measurements were examined descriptively. Four whole-blood transcriptomic cohorts and single-cell data from seven participants provided complementary transcriptional context. LCP1-knockdown THP-1 cells were evaluated after LPS priming and ATP challenge by quantitative PCR, ELISA, ASC imaging, caspase-1 FLICA/propidium iodide flow cytometry, LDH release, and CCK-8, with MCC950 comparison and an LCP1-rescue condition. Results The contrast was associated with 30-day mortality in the three internal populations (adjusted odds ratios per standard deviation, 2.10, 2.18, and 2.01) and in PXD055932 (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78). Its incremental AUC was approximately 0.011 when cross-validation was performed within PXD055932 using SOFA, sex, and batch as baseline covariates. LCP1 and HRG were weakly correlated in the internal train and test populations. Whole-blood LCP1 mortality effects were heterogeneous and nonsignificant in random-effects meta-analysis. Single-cell data showed prominent monocyte LCP1 expression, but participant-level priming and damage-context trends did not meet the false-discovery threshold, and the pyroptosis-execution-associated set was not enriched. LCP1 knockdown modestly reduced LPS-induced transcripts and attenuated ATP-associated ASC-speck positivity, caspase-1-associated FLICA/PI responses, LDH release, and IL-1β secretion. The LCP1-rescue condition recovered these responses to different extents. Conclusion An exploratory LCP1-HRG plasma contrast is associated with sepsis mortality across two source studies, with limited additional discrimination beyond clinical covariates. Intracellular LCP1 contributes to inflammasome-associated lytic responses in THP-1 cells.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Circulating tumor cells in solid tumors: biological adaptation, detection technologies, and clinical implications.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Xu K, Niu J, Cui Y, Roy M, Xu K, Liu Y, Lu P, Lu X, Ji Y.
papers.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are rare tumor-derived cells released from primary or metastatic lesions into the bloodstream and represent key intermediates in hematogenous dissemination. As intact cellular components of liquid biopsy, CTCs provide opportunities to investigate tumor heterogeneity, metastatic evolution, therapeutic resistance, and dynamic molecular alterations that may not be fully captured by tissue biopsy or circulating cell-free analytes. This review summarizes current advances in the biological mechanisms, detection technologies, and clinical applications of CTCs in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on their adaptive responses within the circulation. CTCs exhibit substantial phenotypic and metabolic plasticity, including epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, altered energy metabolism, and enhanced resistance to oxidative and mechanical stress. Their interactions with platelets, neutrophils, and other immune components can further promote survival, immune evasion, and metastatic competence, particularly through the formation of homotypic and heterotypic CTC clusters. Technological advances in antigen-independent enrichment, microfluidic isolation, single-cell multi-omics, and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis are progressively extending CTC assessment beyond enumeration toward molecular and functional characterization. Emerging clinical evidence supports the potential value of CTCs for prognostic stratification, treatment monitoring, and biomarker assessment in breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, and head and neck cancers, although clinical utility varies considerably among tumor types and platforms. Further standardization and prospective validation, together with integration of metabolic, immune, and multi-omic CTC features, will be essential to establish their role in precision oncology.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and triple negative breast cancer: can pathomics help oncologists?
papers.authors: Faa G, Lai E, Suri JS, Solinas C, Dessì M, Saba G, Loi F, Tiwari E, Cau F, Dessena M, Ziranu P, Pretta A, Codipietro C, Graziano S, Saba L, Scartozzi M.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive and heterogeneous subtype of breast cancer with limited targeted therapies and poor prognosis. Recent advances in digital pathology and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming traditional, qualitative histopathology into quantitative, data-driven analysis. Within computational pathology, pathomics (the extraction of handcrafted, high-dimensional features from digitized histological images) and deep learning (DL)-based whole-slide image analysis have been investigated for the prediction of molecular subtypes, biomarker expression, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, and treatment response in TNBC. AI models, including DL and multimodal systems integrating histopathology, omics, and clinical data, are being explored for patient stratification, risk assessment, and therapy personalization, encompassing chemotherapy, immunotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. By linking spatial tissue architecture with molecular profiles, these approaches may provide new insights into tumor biology and the tumor microenvironment. Most TNBC-specific studies are retrospective, small or single-center, few have been externally validated and, to our knowledge, none has yet demonstrated clinical utility in prospective trials; prediction of biomarkers such as PD-L1 or homologous recombination deficiency from hematoxylin and eosin slides remains investigational and cannot replace validated testing. Despite these challenges, AI-assisted computational pathology is a promising decision-support tool, which complements and does not replace pathologists and oncologists, for enhancing diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic decision-making in TNBC.

papers.title: Extracellular galectin-3 preferentially through CD44 and PD-1 binds activated T cells and marks memory-phenotype T cell subsets.
papers.authors: Abouda A, Alimo ET, Azimi A, Bigleri A, Rahmati A, Shahbaz S, Elahi S.
papers.abstract: Background Galectin-3 (Gal-3) is a multifunctional β-galactoside-binding lectin implicated in immune regulation, yet its association with T cell phenotypes under physiological and inflammatory conditions remains incompletely defined. Methods We investigated Gal-3 expression and binding on murine and human T cells across developmental stages, tissues, sex, genetic background, circadian time, and inflammatory disease settings. Results In mice, Gal-3-associated CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were dynamically regulated by age, anatomical location, strain, sex, and circadian rhythm. Gal-3 + T cells displayed increased activation markers, enhanced TCR-associated signaling molecules, elevated cytolytic mediators, increased proliferation, and greater apoptosis. Gal-3 + T cells were enriched within central and effector memory compartments and expressed higher levels of co-inhibitory receptors, including PD-1, with ImageStream analysis confirming Gal-3 co-expressed with PD-1. Recombinant Gal-3 preferentially bound activated, but not resting T cells, and associated with CD44 and CD3, suggesting activation-dependent acquisition of extracellular Gal-3. Re-analysis of human thymocyte and Long COVID single-cell RNA-seq datasets further supported an association between LGALS3 expression and activated/exhausted T cell states. Finally, intracellular staining indicated that T cells are unlikely to be a major source of Gal-3. Conclusion Our findings identify Gal-3 as a context-dependent marker and potential regulator of activated, antigen-experienced T cells, which promotes T cell apoptosis.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis identifies a PLAUR-centered macrophage-associated programmed cell death signature in type A aortic dissection.
papers.authors: Chen T, Zhang Y, Yang X, Bin S, Cheng J, Lei M.
papers.abstract: Background Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening aortic emergency characterized by inflammatory remodeling, extracellular matrix disruption, and programmed cell death (PCD). The cell-specific transcriptional features associated with immune activation and PCD-related aortic wall injury remain incompletely defined. This study investigated PCD-associated immune remodeling in TAAD and evaluated PLAUR as a macrophage-associated marker linked to these pathological changes. Methods Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing, curated PCD-related gene sets, immune deconvolution, pathway enrichment, in silico perturbation analysis, and histological assessment of human aortic specimens. Results TAAD tissues exhibited marked transcriptomic alterations, with 2,217 genes meeting the exploratory differential-expression criteria, accompanied by increased PCD-related transcriptional activity. Single-cell analysis indicated that macrophage-enriched clusters showed relatively high PCD-related gene-set activity, while PLAUR transcripts were predominantly detected in macrophage-enriched clusters. PLAUR was upregulated in TAAD in both training and external validation datasets and strongly correlated with sample-level PCD scores. In the training dataset, PLAUR expression showed exploratory discrimination between TAAD and control tissue samples, with an AUC of 0.858. PLAUR-high samples showed enrichment of HIF-1, JAK-STAT, necroptosis, and apoptosis-related pathways. Immune deconvolution indicated relatively higher neutrophil- and M0 macrophage-associated signatures in TAAD, with PLAUR expression positively associated with myeloid-cell-related features. In silico perturbation analysis identified cytoskeletal and actin-related transcriptional changes associated with predicted PLAUR perturbation. Histological assessment demonstrated aortic wall disorganization, collagen remodeling, elastic fiber disruption, increased TUNEL positivity, and elevated PLAUR protein expression in TAAD lesions. Conclusions PLAUR is associated with macrophage-enriched inflammatory, proteolytic, and PCD-related remodeling in TAAD and may serve as a candidate marker of these pathological features. The present findings are associative and do not establish a causal role for PLAUR in aortic wall degeneration or dissection initiation. Spatially resolved and functional studies are required to determine whether PLAUR-positive macrophage states contribute mechanistically to TAAD pathogenesis.

papers.title: A practical workflow for isolation and low-input multi-omic and functional profiling of neutrophils from tumor tissue.
papers.authors: Ugolini A, De Leo A, Yu X, Veglia F.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated neutrophils (TAN) are increasingly recognized as major regulators of tumor progression, metastasis, immune suppression, and response to immunotherapy. However, mechanistic studies of TAN remain technically challenging due to the frequently limited numbers recoverable from individual tumor specimens, susceptibility to activation during tissue processing, rapid apoptosis ex vivo , and poor survival following fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS). These limitations often compromise downstream molecular and functional analyses and contribute to substantial variability between laboratories. Importantly, the difficulty of recovering highly viable TAN has also limited direct functional validation of neutrophil states identified by transcriptomic profiling, leading many studies to infer functional heterogeneity primarily from transcriptional signatures. Here, we describe a practical workflow for the isolation of highly viable TAN from murine and human solid tumors. The protocol combines gentle tissue dissociation, sterile low-stress cell sorting conditions, post-sort handling, and downstream applications including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with bioinformatic considerations, bulk RNA sequencing, CUT&RUN epigenomic profiling, mini suppression assays, ex vivo cultures, real time quantitative PCR and western blotting. Particular emphasis is placed on pre-analytical variables that critically affect TAN viability and on neutrophil-specific considerations for scRNA-seq quality control and interpretation. The workflow is designed to be adaptable to different tumor types and enables robust characterization of low-frequency neutrophil populations that are typically difficult to study using conventional approaches, facilitating experimental validation of the biological functions associated with transcriptionally defined TAN states.

papers.title: From chronic airway injury to lung cancer: epithelial memory, field cancerization, and premalignant evolution.
papers.authors: Wang W, Ji X, Chang Z.
papers.abstract: Chronic airway injury induced by tobacco smoke, environmental pollutants, and persistent inflammatory lung diseases provides a biological foundation for lung carcinogenesis, yet the cellular and molecular trajectory from repeated epithelial damage to invasive malignancy has only recently come into focus. Here we synthesize three interconnected concepts that together define this trajectory: epithelial memory, the capacity of airway basal and secretory cells to retain epigenetic and transcriptional scars long after the initial insult has ceased; field cancerization, whereby histologically normal-appearing airway epithelium harbours widespread clonal alterations that expand the pool of at-risk cells; and premalignant evolution, the Darwinian selection and diversification of clones as genetic, epigenetic, immune, and metabolic pressures reshape the altered field. We review evidence from single-cell genomics, spatial transcriptomics, and longitudinal human cohort studies that reveals how smoking-associated DNA methylation marks, persistent chromatin accessibility changes, and rewired transcriptional programmes establish an epigenetically primed epithelial landscape. Within this landscape, somatic driver mutations in TP53, KRAS, NOTCH1, and chromatin remodelling genes confer competitive fitness advantages, enabling clonal expansion across large territories of the bronchial tree. We propose an integrative model in which epigenetic priming, somatic mutation, clonal competition, immune surveillance, and metabolic constraints interact over years to decades, without assuming a universal fixed sequence across all lung cancer subtypes. This framework identifies actionable interception windows - from epigenetic reversal of injury memory to targeted elimination of premalignant clones - and highlights the need for longitudinal single-cell atlases and lineage-resolved models to resolve the causal ordering of molecular events. We conclude that lung cancer is best understood not as an abrupt cellular transformation but as the end point of a protracted, spatially distributed evolutionary process whose earliest stages may be reversible.

papers.title: MIF and CXCL8 shape inflammatory myeloid-epithelial crosstalk in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a machine learning and integrative transcriptomic investigation.
papers.authors: Wang W, Li X, Li J, Zhou S, Ma X, Ren J, Zhang S.
papers.abstract: Background Progression from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) to cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is accompanied by extensive epithelial remodeling and changes in the inflammatory immune microenvironment. However, how stage-specific epithelial states interact with inflammatory myeloid responses, spatial immune organization, and patient prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated these changes and identified inflammation-related molecular features associated with clinical outcome. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic and survival cohorts, and drug-response data were integrated. Stage-associated cell states, epithelial trajectories, gene co-expression programs, and predicted cell-cell communication were analyzed across normal cervical tissue, HSIL, and squamous cell carcinoma. Machine-learning survival models were developed in TCGA-CESC and evaluated in GSE39001, GSE52903, and CGCI-HTMCP-CC. Pathway enrichment and immune deconvolution were used to assess biological and immune features associated with the prognostic model. Drug-response prediction, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and immunohistochemistry provided additional computational and tissue-level evaluation. Results HSIL was characterized by a proliferative epithelial state, whereas SCC was enriched for an epithelial state associated with keratinization stress, interferon responses, and inferred copy-number abnormalities, accompanied by increased inflammatory myeloid populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed stronger immune and myeloid programs at the invasive front than in the tumor core. Predicted epithelial-myeloid communication in SCC prominently involved MIF-CD74 receptor complexes and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling. A five-gene prognostic model consisting of MIF, SPP1, CXCL8, CALML5, and CD74 achieved C-indices of 0.748, 0.696, and 0.691 in TCGA-CESC, GSE39001, and GSE52903, respectively. Higher risk scores were associated with hypoxia, glycolysis, TGF-β/EMT signaling, stromal remodeling, and reduced adaptive immune programs. MK-2206 showed favorable predicted interactions with MIF and CXCL8, with greater modeled stability for the CXCL8 complex. Immunohistochemistry confirmed progressively increased CXCL8 and MIF expression from normal cervix to HSIL and SCC. Conclusion Progression from HSIL to SCC was associated with coordinated epithelial remodeling, inflammatory myeloid activation, and spatial reorganization of the immune microenvironment. MIF-CD74 and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling were implicated in epithelial-myeloid communication, while the five-gene inflammatory model showed reproducible prognostic performance across independent cohorts. These results support further investigation of MIF- and CXCL8-related inflammatory signaling in cervical cancer progression and prognosis.

papers.title: An integrative analysis of transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing data identifies cytoskeleton-related prognostic genes in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhang S, Song M, Wei B, Liu Z, Hu Z, Hu D.
papers.abstract: Background Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an aggressive malignancy with dismal prognosis, primarily attributed to substantial tumor heterogeneity. Although the cytoskeleton is critically implicated in cancer progression, a comprehensive characterization of cytoskeleton-related prognostic genes in ESCC is still absent. Methods Bulk transcriptome data from public repositories were integrated with a single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset for comprehensive analysis. Cytoskeleton-related candidate genes were screened by intersecting differentially expressed genes with a curated cytoskeleton-related gene (CRG) list, and expression findings were experimentally corroborated in clinical specimens via real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Independent prognostic genes were subsequently determined through univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses and incorporated into a risk model, which was subsequently evaluated in two external cohorts. Additional analyses covered functional enrichment, immune infiltration profiling, drug sensitivity estimation, mutational landscape characterization, and single-cell-level investigations of inferred metabolic pathway activity, intercellular communication, and differentiation trajectories. Results A total of 222 cytoskeleton-related candidate genes were identified. Among these, three genes -GABARAPL2, PDLIM2, and PPP2R2A - were established as independent prognostic factors and incorporated into a robust risk-scoring model. This model reliably partitioned patients into high- and low-risk groups with markedly divergent survival outcomes, and a similar association between the risk score and survival was observed in two external cohorts. The high-risk group exhibited distinct estimated immune infiltration, immune checkpoint expression, somatic mutation, and predicted drug sensitivity profiles. scRNA-seq analysis characterized the distribution of the prognostic genes across cell types and supported the selection of T cells for further exploratory analyses of metabolism, intercellular communication, and differentiation trajectories. Conclusion This multi-omics integrative study identified and validated a CRG signature with potential prognostic value in ESCC and revealed its associations with immune microenvironment features and computationally predicted drug response patterns. These findings support the potential utility of the signature for risk stratification and provide testable hypotheses for further investigation of ESCC biology.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies stem-like subpopulations and their gene signature in lung adenocarcinoma progression.
papers.authors: Shao L, Guo J, Chen Y, Wu H, Zhong Y, Dong J, Huang W, Sun Y, Yang J, Chen S, He Q.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) demonstrates significant intra-tumor heterogeneity (ITH), which plays a critical role in disease progression and complicates therapeutic interventions. In the present study, we employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to analyze cellular populations derived from stage I and stage III LUAD tumors, alongside matched adjacent normal tissues, with the objective of delineating malignant cell states and identifying tumor-propagating subpopulations. Unsupervised clustering analysis identified eight principal cell lineages, with epithelial cells predominating within tumor samples. Notably, advanced-stage tumors demonstrated a shift toward an immunosuppressive microenvironment, characterized by elevated T cell exhaustion and an increased presence of pro-angiogenic macrophages. Further stratification of malignant cells revealed eleven distinct subclusters, with stage III tumors enriched for invasive and immunosuppressive phenotypes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis identified evolutionary transitions from alveolar-like states toward squamous and stress-responsive lineages. Employing CytoTRACE to evaluate stemness independently of predefined markers, we identified subpopulations of cancer stem cells (sub-CSCs) predominantly in stage III tumors. These sub-CSCs exhibited heightened transcriptional heterogeneity and a core gene signature associated with cytoskeletal motility, immune regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and protein homeostasis. A four-gene panel derived from this signature demonstrated robust prognostic significance in independent LUAD cohorts. Collectively, these findings enhance the current understanding of stemness-driven tumor progression in LUAD and suggest potential therapeutic targets to address tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: Targeting pyroptosis: therapeutic potential in the immune-inflammatory imbalance of chronic kidney disease.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Wu X, Liu W, Long M, Zeng L, Dai A.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is sustained by interacting metabolic, hemodynamic, immune, and fibrotic pathways, yet the contribution of pyroptosis differs substantially across renal compartments and disease contexts. Pyroptosis is a gasdermin-dependent lytic form of regulated cell death that can couple intrinsic renal-cell injury to the release of interleukin-1β, interleukin-18, and damage-associated molecular patterns. This review critically evaluates the evidence linking inflammasome-caspase-gasdermin signaling to diabetic kidney disease, lupus nephritis, IgA nephropathy and membranous nephropathy, crystalline nephropathy, and renal fibrosis. A structured evidence-mapping approach was used to distinguish mechanistic findings from in vitro systems and animal models from observations in human kidney tissue and interventional clinical evidence. Across CKD phenotypes, human studies support pathway activation and cell-type-specific associations, whereas most causal evidence for pyroptosis itself derives from experimental models; this distinction is essential because inflammasome activation or cytokine elevation alone does not establish gasdermin-mediated lytic cell death. Therapeutically, NLRP3, inflammatory caspases, and GSDMD remain attractive targets, but renal translation is still early. Agents such as MCC950, VX-765, disulfiram, and kidney-targeted delivery systems have shown benefit predominantly in preclinical models. The AI-screened GSDMD pore blocker SK56 provides an important proof of concept for effector-stage inhibition, although it has not yet been validated as a CKD therapy. Early clinical development of NLRP3 inhibition in patients with CKD further underscores both the opportunity and the need for rigorous target-engagement, safety, and renal-outcome studies. Future progress will depend on human-anchored biomarkers of gasdermin activation, spatial and single-cell resolution of disease-specific cell states, models that better reproduce multimorbid CKD, and trials that balance anti-inflammatory efficacy against the physiological roles of inflammasome signaling in host defense and tissue repair.

papers.title: Granzyme K associates with inflammatory immune programs and B-cell dysregulation in systemic lupus erythematosus.
papers.authors: Pu Y, Chen Z, Yang P, Zhu Q, Long H, Zhou Y, Deng D.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease characterized by systemic immune activation and multi-organ inflammation. Granzyme K (GZMK), a serine protease predominantly expressed by CD8 + T cells and natural killer cells, has emerging non-cytotoxic inflammatory functions, but its relevance to SLE remains incompletely defined. In this study, we conducted investigations using plasma and tissue analyses, single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, an animal model, and primary human B cell experiments. Plasma GZMK was increased in patients with SLE and was associated with clinical disease activity. Integrated multi-tissue single cell analysis identified preferential GZMK enrichment in CD8 + effector memory T (Tem) cells and a higher relative abundance of this compartment in SLE, while proteomic profiling and multiplex immunofluorescence provided protein and tissue level evidence for a GZMK-enriched CD8 + memory T cell population. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested enhanced predicted communication between Tem and B lineage cells, and circulating GZMK was further associated with a plasma cell-like population. In two murine models, PPACK, which can inhibit GZMK catalytic activity but is not GZMK selective, attenuated lupus associated inflammatory phenotypes and partially normalized altered splenic B cell composition. In vitro experiments showed that active recombinant GZMK augmented plasma-cell-associated phenotypic and transcriptional responses under B cell expansion conditions. Collectively, these findings identify circulating GZMK as an independent correlate of SLE clinical activity and characterize a recurrent GZMK-enriched CD8 + memory/Tem cell program across peripheral blood and affected tissues that is associated with B-cell dysregulation and plasma-cell-related immune abnormalities.

papers.title: Single-cell analyses identify persistent neuroimmune remodeling and prioritize SPP1 and LGALS3 in neuropathic pain.
papers.authors: Li J, Ma S, Ye K, Zhang B.
papers.abstract: Introduction Persistent neuropathic pain involves lasting sensory and immune changes. We examined which expression programs persist across injury settings and whether prioritized genes are associated with pain severity. Methods We analyzed five public single-cell or single-nucleus transcriptomic resources and two independent bulk RNA-sequencing resources, then examined tissue expression and behavior in spared nerve injury experiments. Results Microglial expression showed a distinct early response and persistent glial-program activity. The glial signature remained elevated at day 14 and month 5 after exclusion of Spp1 and Lgals3 (false-discovery-adjusted q=0.0473 and 0.00128). Independent bulk data supported neuronal injury-related and glial programs, although candidate-gene effects varied across populations and stages. Spp1 and Lgals3 retained high priority in ranking sensitivity analyses, and their dorsal root ganglion expression correlated with mechanical hypersensitivity after adjustment for collection endpoint. Post-injury Lumogallion treatment increased the day-14 paw-withdrawal threshold (treated/vehicle geometric-mean ratio 4.08, 95% confidence interval 2.53-6.55) and reduced selected dorsal root ganglion and spinal transcripts. Structural modeling proposed an LGALS3-Lumogallion interaction for experimental testing. Discussion These findings link persistent neuroimmune expression programs to tissue-level Spp1 and Lgals3 associations and show partial behavioral improvement with Lumogallion. Direct target-engagement studies are planned to determine whether LGALS3 contributes to this response.

papers.title: Tertiary lymphoid structures in luminal gastrointestinal cancers: biological circuits, spatial architecture, and biomarkers in the perioperative immunotherapy era.
papers.authors: Sun S, Chen J, Zhong Y, Luo Y, Zhang G.
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are inducible, organized lymphoid clusters that recapitulate key functions of secondary lymphoid organs within chronically inflamed tumor tissue. In colorectal, gastric, and esophageal cancers, the most common luminal gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies, surgical resection preserves the spatial relationship between TLS and the tumor core, invasive margin, and surrounding mucosa, making the resected specimen a uniquely informative anchor for studying antitumor immunity. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from human cohorts, single-cell and spatial genomics, and perioperative immunotherapy trials. We trace the developmental continuum from loose lymphocytic clusters to germinal center-bearing follicles, contrast germinal center-dependent humoral immunity with germinal center-independent B-cell responses, and examine how regulatory T and B cells can turn TLS into immunosuppressive niches. We then analyze proposed inductive circuits, including chemokine-stromal organization, microbial and mutational antigenic pressure, and innate immune sensing, and discuss how desmoplasia, mechanical compression, hypoxia, and metabolic competition may arrest TLS maturation. A tumor-by-tumor comparison of colorectal, gastric, and esophageal cancers shows that TLS density, maturity, and anatomic localization carry divergent prognostic information; and diffuse gastric cancer, peritoneal metastases, and chemoradiated esophageal tumors illustrate states of TLS disruption. We also appraise neoadjuvant checkpoint trials (NICHE, NICHE-2, NEONIPIGA, CheckMate 577, MATTERHORN), consider TLS as complements to TNM staging for adjuvant decision-making and as candidate correlates of pathologic response, and outline experimental strategies for TLS induction and the technical prerequisites for translating TLS into surgical biomarkers. We hypothesize that mature, margin-positioned TLS are promising development- and location-dependent markers of organized antitumor immunity, but routine clinical use awaits standardized, multicenter validation. We therefore propose a minimum reporting framework to accelerate this translation.

papers.title: CFTR regulation of ROS-mediated cellular injury and immune dysregulation in cystic fibrosis.
papers.authors: Shi C, Zhang M, Wang H, Jiao Y, Wang X, Chen Y, Ma C, Shi J.
papers.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-limiting autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, most commonly F508del. Mutant CFTR disrupts transepithelial ion transport and intracellular redox homeostasis, leading to excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Evidence from cohort studies, human airway organoid models, and single-cell transcriptomic analyses published between 2020 and 2026 has prompted substantial revision of the prevailing linear model of CF pathogenesis. These studies demonstrate that misfolded CFTR can independently initiate oxidative stress and low-grade inflammation in the absence of microbial colonization. Mitochondrial ROS (mitoROS) constitute a central signaling hub linking F508del-induced protein misfolding to transcriptional suppression of the Nrf2 antioxidant program, constitutive activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and dysregulation of TLR-cytokine cascades. Triple CFTR modulator regimens, including elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) and the once-daily combination vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (Alyftrek, FDA-approved December 2024 for patients ≥6 years carrying at least one F508del or other Alyftrek-responsive CFTR variant; pivotal SKYLINE 102/103 trials demonstrated non-inferiority versus ETI in largely ETI-eligible populations), have transformed clinical care. However, multi-omics data indicate that these agents do not fully restore airway redox homeostasis or resolve persistent low-grade inflammation, even when CFTR channel activity recovers to 40%-50% of wild-type levels. This incomplete recovery may reflect persistent epigenetic inflammatory memory, uncorrected mitochondrial dysfunction, and incomplete restoration of the non-channel functions of CFTR. Moreover, marked interindividual variability in modulator response and persistent nonresponse underscore the need for adjunctive strategies. This review integrates foundational mechanistic studies with recent findings to delineate how CFTR regulates ROS-dependent tissue injury and immune dysregulation and to assess redox-targeted combination therapies designed to complement CFTR modulator monotherapy.

papers.title: Identification and monitoring of immune-related adverse reactions of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors based on symptom network analysis.
papers.authors: Gao Y, Wang Y, Yu L.
papers.abstract: Background PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors have become first-line cancer therapies by disrupting immune checkpoint downregulation, thereby potentiating antitumor immunity. However, this enhanced immune activation may also target normal tissues, triggering multisystemic immune-related adverse events (irAE) that complicate clinical management. Conventional pharmacovigilance analyses typically assess individual adverse events in isolation, limiting the ability to capture inter-symptom relationships. Symptom network analysis, an emerging computational approach, constructs co-occurrence networks to identify core symptoms, key associations, and bridge nodes across organ systems, thus enabling a systematic understanding of complex suspected irAE profiles. Methods Adverse event records for six PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors were extracted from two spontaneous reporting databases: FAERS (Q1 2005-Q3 2024) and JADER (Q1 2004-Q1 2025). Potential signals were screened using reporting odds ratio(ROR), proportional reporting ratio(PRR), and multivariate gamma-Poisson shrinkage (MGPS) methods. Symptom co-occurrence networks were subsequently constructed using EBIC-GLASSO based on Tetrachoric correlation matrices, which are specifically designed for binary adverse event data and correct for attenuation due to dichotomization. Four centrality metrics-Strength, Closeness, Betweenness, and Expected Influence-were calculated via the qgraph package. The bootnet package performed 1,000 bootstrap iterations to evaluate 95% confidence intervals for edge weights and centrality stability coefficients. Results In FAERS, nivolumab (48,330) and pembrolizumab (37,224) generated the highest report volumes. PD-1 inhibitor networks consistently centered on a systemic-gastrointestinal symptom cluster comprising decreased appetite, fatigue, diarrhea, and nausea, whereas PD-L1 inhibitor networks additionally featured prominent hematologic abnormalities. In JADER, interstitial lung disease and adrenal insufficiency emerged as central nodes, reflecting cross-database differences in reporting patterns and physician-initiated reporting practices. Strength and Expected Influence centrality metrics showed good to excellent stability (CS ≥ 0.672 in most networks), supporting the robustness of the core symptom clusters. Conclusion Symptom network analysis effectively delineates core suspected irAE symptoms and inter-system associations for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. FAERS-derived networks emphasize systemic-gastrointestinal syndromes, while JADER reveals pulmonary-endocrine predominance in Japanese populations. These findings demonstrate the utility of symptom network analysis as a complementary approach to traditional pharmacovigilance for characterizing complex suspected irAE patterns across different data sources and populations.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant treatment is associated with fibrotic and transcriptional remodeling of tumor-draining lymph nodes in rectal cancer.
papers.authors: Shi Y, Zhao Z, Li Y, Cheng Z, Niu Y, Zhang J, Liu H, Zou S, Zhang Z, Chen H, Guan X, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Background Neoadjuvant treatment is associated with reduced lymph-node yield in rectal cancer, but the accompanying changes in tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) remain incompletely characterized. Methods We analyzed Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data, a 178-patient institutional cohort, quantitative histopathology of 447 histologically negative TDLNs from 159 patients, and bulk RNA sequencing of 30 nodes from 24 patients. Institutional comparisons distinguished a radiotherapy-containing treatment pathway (RT) from management without preoperative radiotherapy (NRT); in the institutional clinical cohort, all 105 RT patients and 10 of 73 NRT patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Pathology models accounted for patient clustering, and RNA counts were aggregated within patients. Results Recorded preoperative radiotherapy was associated with lower examined-node counts in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER). In the institutional cohort, the expanded pretreatment-adjusted incidence-rate ratio was 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.67-1.02]; pretreatment-covariate overlap weighting yielded 0.80 (95% CI, 0.66-0.96). RT-group nodes were more fibrotic and smaller, with lower germinal-center and lymphoid-tissue area fractions. Patient-level RNA-seq identified 4,446 differentially expressed genes, with higher extracellular-matrix and angiogenic programs and lower antigen-receptor and B-cell-receptor signaling. Selected pathway directions were retained across sensitivity analyses. Computational deconvolution provided supportive estimates of relative cell composition. Conclusion A radiotherapy-containing neoadjuvant treatment pathway, including chemoradiotherapy in the institutional clinical, pathology, and RNA-seq cohorts, was associated with lower node yield and structural and transcriptional differences in TDLNs. These findings characterize the nodal structural and transcriptional phenotype associated with neoadjuvant treatment.

papers.title: Exploratory integrated analysis of the microbiome and host transcriptome reveals correlations between the intratumoral microbiota and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Yang K, He S, Wang Q, Jin D, Zhang Y, Que C, Lv H, Gou Y.
papers.abstract: Background The intratumoral microbiota can affect the occurrence, development, and prognosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) through various mechanisms. This study explored the relationship between key genes and key microorganisms in ESCC. Methods A systematic multiomic integration pipeline was applied to analyze the transcriptomic and 16S rRNA sequencing data of cancerous and paracancerous tissues obtained from patients with ESCC. Differential expression analysis, protein-protein interaction networks, and machine learning algorithms were successively used to identify key host genes in ESCC. Notably, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune infiltration analysis were employed to investigate relevant mechanisms. Subsequently, differential abundance analysis and machine learning were used to elucidate key intratumoral microorganisms. Finally, a combined multiomic analysis using the Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker discovery using Latent cOmponents (DIABLO) framework and Spearman correlation networks (CIRCOS) was employed to explore synergistic host-microbe associations. Results TNNC2 , CTHRC1 , MMP10 , CGAS , IL18 , SERPINE1 , CCNA1 , and POSTN were identified as key genes. GSEA revealed that key genes were mainly involved in the cell cycle, indicating that cell cycle disorders might affect the progression of ESCC. The enrichment scores of seven types of immune cells significantly changed during ESCC progression. Additionally, 14 differentially abundant microorganisms were detected, and four key microorganisms were identified: Lachnoanaerobaculum , Fusobacterium , Actinomyces , and Capnocytophaga . Among them, Lachnoanaerobaculum was associated with multiple key genes, including POSTN , MMP10 , CTHRC1 , and CGAS . Exploratory DIABLO analysis highlighted concordant variation of the selected transcriptomic and microbiomic features between ESCC and adjacent nontumor tissue tissues. Conclusion Eight host genes and four microbial genera were identified as candidate ESCC-associated features. Given the small cohort and lack of independent validation, these findings should be considered preliminary and confirmation in larger independent cohorts is required.

papers.title: Retrospective analysis of feline heartworm disease ( Dirofilaria immitis ): diagnostic patterns in cats presenting with respiratory or vomiting signs (2013-2023, USA).
papers.authors: Whittle A, Ferguson B, Taylor-Rakocevic M, Poulsen Nautrup B, Topdijan K, Sheehy J, Mwacalimba K.
papers.abstract: Feline heartworm infection, caused by the mosquito-borne nematode Dirofilaria immitis , is a serious and potentially fatal disease in cats. The true prevalence of this infection is likely underestimated due to the nonspecific nature of clinical signs, such as coughing, vomiting, or respiratory distress, and the diagnostic limitations of current feline heartworm antigen (Ag) and antibody (Ab) assays. This study aimed to enhance understanding of its recognition and detection by linking diverse clinical presentations with diagnostic test results. Anonymized feline medical records spanning 10 years from more than 1,000 Banfield U.S. veterinary clinics were analyzed using machine learning methods. Cats were included if records contained respiratory, vomiting, or heartworm-specific diagnostic codes and at least one heartworm Ag or Ab test. Test positivity rates were linked to clinical signs. For cats tested with both assays, concordance between results was assessed. Of 146,111 eligible cats, 91,438 (62.58%) underwent heartworm testing, and 1,555 (1.70%) were positive on at least one assay. Cats with heartworm-specific diagnostic codes had the highest positivity, but those with respiratory or vomiting codes accounted for 7.01 and 10.10% of all positives. Among 127 cats tested with both assays, 24.41% were discordant, mainly Ag-positive/Ab-negative. Heartworm infection should be considered in any cat with respiratory signs (including asthma-like presentations) or vomiting. To improve its detection, both heat-treated Ag and Ab assays should be used to screen cats annually, and in cats presenting with respiratory signs or vomiting.

papers.title: Computational immunogenicity prediction for mRNA vaccines: benchmarks, bottlenecks, and the peptide-nucleotide gap.
papers.authors: Kamaliasl S, Buckley NE, Dunne NJ, McCarthy HO.
papers.abstract: Computational prediction of T-cell epitopes has become indispensable to vaccine design, yet the field still relies on the assumption that how much of a given antigen is produced is fixed by its coding sequence. However, this is not the case with mRNA vaccines, i.e. the design of the mRNA template can vastly alter the quantity of the same protein produced. Codon usage, guanine-cytosine (GC) content, untranslated-region (UTR) design, and predicted secondary structure together define how fast the message is translated and how long it survives, and therefore how much antigen ever reaches the presentation pathway. This is a variable that no current immunogenicity predictor represents. Herein we appraise three decades of computational immunogenicity prediction, tracing the path from position-specific scoring matrices through pan-specific neural networks to transformer-based protein language models, and we use that history to expose the peptide-nucleotide gap between these tools and the way mRNA vaccines are designed. A structured synthesis of published evaluations of leading predictors across human leukocyte antigen (HLA) alleles, peptide lengths and data types shows that headline accuracy masks persistent deficiencies in predicting major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II, which underpins durable T-cell help, and rare alleles, which disproportionately affect under-represented populations. Four bottlenecks continue to constrain the field: class II prediction, T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition, immunodominance, and the disconnection between nucleotide-level design and peptide-level prediction. We argue that the last of these, which has drawn the least attention, is, in our assessment, the most likely to yield near-term gains for personalised cancer vaccines and pandemic preparedness, and we set out an architecture that couples translation-rate prediction to peptide presentation. Building it will require data that do not yet exist; we specify what must be measured, and on which platforms.

papers.title: Integrin-Related Gene Signatures in Ewing Sarcoma Prognosis and Immune Microenvironment Analysis Using Bioinformatics and LASSO Regression.
papers.authors: Cui C, Yu B, Si Y, Zhang Y, Shen Y, Liu J, Cao Y.
papers.abstract: Objectives To identify integrin-related genes (IRGs) as potential prognostic indicators for Ewing sarcoma (ES), a rare, aggressive malignancy of children and adolescents associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment efficacy, particularly in metastatic disease. Methods The Gene Expression Omnibus datasets GSE17674 and GSE17679 were used for bioinformatics analyses as the training and validation datasets, respectively. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened and subjected to functional enrichment analysis. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to identify characteristic genes, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis to assess diagnostic potential, and CIBERSORT to analyze immune cell infiltration. Results Of the 9,846 DEGs identified in GSE17674, 15 were IRGs with significant differences in expression (p 0.9, indicating high diagnostic value. Immune cell infiltration analysis showed increased M0 macrophages and activated mast cells in ES samples. Conclusions IRGs play a pivotal role in ES progression and regulation of the immune microenvironment; these findings provide insight into the molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets. Reliance on public databases and the absence of in vitro and in vivo experimental validation are limitations shared by retrospective bioinformatics studies. Further experimental validation is needed.
